Anthropic.content:
ISSUE NO.

11

·

# The Week in AI

## Our weekly read on the AI stories that matter to the people building the future enterprise.

Anthropic has released Claude Fable 5.2, open to everyone, and Mythos 5.2, which has looser cyber-security guardrails and is limited to certified companies. Anthropic reports clear gains in coding, reasoning and science, plus new robotics abilities, and a lower price per token. Its own charts compare Fable at extra-high effort against older models.

Spotted on

Anthropic

### Why it matters for you

The change I notice most is that coding quality now holds when you move from research into building, so a hard problem can be quickly iterated in one model. It also writes far more readably than 5.1, though it shows less of its reasoning, so I'd keep a person checking the work that matters. The lower price per token only holds at lower effort settings. Anthropic's own charts show it costing more than the previous model above high effort. Fable is also more capable than most work requires. I’d gate access to the work that needs it, set effort defaults centrally and use cheaper models for routine jobs.

Anthropic has launched Claude Meetings, which joins video calls to draft plans, answer questions and record actions, alongside Claude Whiteboards and Claude Sheets. Together with Claude Docs, they move Claude towards a full office suite. The launch also adds wider data and app integrations.

Spotted on

TechCrunch

### Why it matters for you

Put a circle around meetings, documents, spreadsheets and whiteboards and you have most of what people use every day. I read this as Anthropic accepting that the model alone is no longer a defence, so the suite is there to give you more reasons to stay within their ecosystem. Smaller and younger firms without long incumbent contracts will be tempted, but a large enterprise won't leave Microsoft 365 for this - yet. When Anthropic ship their own identity and email services, it may be worth a serious look when your next renewal comes around.

Deloitte surveyed 806 board members and C-suite executives in 53 countries. Only 16% have an established strategy for how technology change affects their workforce, and almost half say boards don't consistently bring people into AI discussions. Productivity dominates board conversations, while employee trust comes up in only 6%.

### Why it matters for you

Fewer than one in five organisations have a plan for what AI means for their people, and employee trust comes up in only six in a hundred board conversations. Boards are signing off AI spend without discussing what it means for the workforce. That's a governance gap, and it's one we hear about in client conversations. Closing it has to start at the top, because people copy their leaders, and nobody uses the tools with confidence if senior leaders don't. Our advice is to put the AI programme and the people plan under one owner.

OpenAI has launched a beta that lets verified businesses claim and manage a ChatGPT profile, add product feeds with pricing, and see aggregated mentions and clicks. Businesses can also set up an agent that answers for them and pay to sponsor it through ChatGPT Ads. It starts with US e-commerce.

Spotted on

Dataconomy

### Why it matters for you

A business can now have an agent speaking for it inside ChatGPT, and paying to be seen there has arrived. It's US e-commerce only for now, but I'd expect it to spread. Someone has to own that agent and decide what it's allowed to say, so this is a brand and governance question as much as a marketing one. I'd settle it before the profile goes live, the same way you'd sign off a spokesperson. Earn your place through sources others cite, because self-published "best of" lists won't hold up for long.

Anthropic.title: Anthropic releases Claude Fable and Mythos 5.2 shortly before record-breaking IPO
Anthropic.description: Claude Fable Gets a Price Cut Anthropic releases Claude Fable and Mythos 5.2 shortly before record-breaking IPO ... Anthropic updated its most capable public model and removed safeguards for its private twin, opening Claude Mythos to more organizations that apply for access.
Anthropic.content:
# Claude Fable Gets a Price Cut Anthropic releases Claude Fable and Mythos 5.2 shortly before record-breaking IPO

Published

Reading time

5 min read

Anthropic updated its most capable public model and removed safeguards for its private twin, opening Claude Mythos to more organizations that apply for access. Meanwhile, the company began selling shares to the public for the first time at a market capitalization of $1.5 trillion.

What’s new: Anthropic introduced Claude Fable 5.2, which costs 20 percent less per token than Claude Fable 5.1. Claude Mythos 5.2, a version with fewer biology and cybersecurity safeguards, is available only to organizations that Anthropic approves.

- Undisclosed: Parameter count, architecture, training data and methods
- Weights/license: Proprietary
- Price: Via API 8/0.20/$40 per million input/cached/output tokens with cache writes at 10/16 per million tokens for five-minute/one-hour caches and 50 percent off for batched requests; fast mode 16/80 per million input/output token.
- Availability: Claude Fable 5.2 via Claude apps on eligible paid plans, Claude Code, Claude API, Amazon Bedrock, Claude Platform on AWS, Claude Models on Google Cloud, and Microsoft Foundry, with 30-day data retention required; Claude Mythos 5.2 only to organizations approved through Anthropic’s Cyber Verification Program or Life Sciences Verification Program
- Performance: First on Artificial Analysis’ Intelligence Index v5.0.1 (65), Vals AI’s Vals Index (71.31 percent), and ARC Prize’s ARC-AGI-3 in its standard harness (81.2 percent)
- Knowledge cutoff: June 2026
- Features: Reasoning always on, with five reasoning levels (low, medium, high, xhigh, max), defaults to high in API and medium in Claude apps and Claude Code; tool use; fast mode, which generates tokens up to 2.5 times faster
- Input/output: Text and images in (up to 1 million tokens), text out (up to 128,000 tokens, 112 tokens per second)

How it works: Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2 are one model with different safeguards. Anthropic described one change to how it trained the model and several to how it restricts the model’s use.

- Another anti-distillation measure, which Anthropic calls “preserved thinking” and now applies to all API accounts rather than only new ones, stops anyone from editing earlier turns of a conversation to extract the model’s reasoning.
- To deter distillation (training a model on another model’s outputs), Anthropic added protections, such as showing users only a summary of the model’s reasoning. Claude models now screen requests that try to extract these traces. The company says this cuts the data distillers collect by 90 to 99 percent.
- In Claude Fable 5.2, classifiers block high-risk cybersecurity work such as penetration testing (simulated attacks on a system to find vulnerabilities) and generating exploits. Blocked requests route to older models: Claude Opus 4.8 answers barred cybersecurity requests, and Claude Opus 5 answers barred biology requests and a small set of requests about developing AI models. Anthropic says the cybersecurity and biology classifiers are as robust as Claude Fable 5.1’s but block about 55 percent fewer requests; the company describes these as legitimate requests blocked by mistake.
- During training, Anthropic limited the model’s progress in two skills that can speed development of AI models: optimizing kernels for AI chips and improving large language model architectures. Anthropic says the model performs at about the level of Claude Opus 5.5 in these areas, and that related skills such as agentic coding, hardware development, and “traditional” machine learning research were not limited.

Performance: Claude Fable 5.2 ranks first on independent intelligence leaderboards from Artificial Analysis and Vals AI, but its cost per task is the highest of any model Artificial Analysis has priced. In Anthropic’s tests, Fable 5.2 improved most (relative to its predecessor) on a test of paid freelance projects.

- In Anthropic’s tests on the Remote Labor Index, 240 paid freelance projects in areas such as game development, architecture, and data analysis, Claude Fable 5.2 set to high reasoning produced work that human evaluators judged at least as good as the freelancers’ on 41.3 percent of projects, leading all models with more than twice the success rate of Claude Fable 5.1.
- On Arena AI’s Agent Arena, which ranks models by how they perform in real user sessions based on task success, user satisfaction, and steerability, Claude Fable 5.2 ranks first, ahead of Claude Opus 5.5. It also leads Agent Arena’s coding category (33.17 percent net improvement). On Arena AI’s WebDev leaderboard, which ranks models via blind head-to-head comparisons of websites they build, Claude Fable 5.2 ranks first (1,826 Elo) narrowly ahead of Claude Opus 5.5 (1,816 Elo).
- On Vals AI’s Vals Index, which combines eight tests of finance, coding, legal, and tax work, Claude Fable 5.2 set to max reasoning ranks first (71.31 percent accuracy, $17.94 and 43.7 minutes per test), ahead of Claude Sonnet 5.5 (70.85, $16.18 and 86 minutes per test) and Gemini 4 Carbon (70.45, $10.51 and 47.75 minutes per test). Among individual tests, it ranks first on Finance Agent v2.1, financial analysis tasks (69.47 percent); EMB v1.1, financial modeling in spreadsheets (77.38 percent); Vibe Code Bench v1.1, building apps from plain-language requests (93.77 percent); ProgramBench, rebuilding programs from scratch (19.00 percent); and BioMysteryBench, biology data investigations developed by Anthropic (83.70 percent). It ties Claude Opus 5.5 on Terminal-Bench 4.0, 66 long tasks in a computer terminal (65.15 percent), and matches several models with a perfect score on ProofBench v1.1, formally verified math proofs.
- On Artificial Analysis’ Intelligence Index v5.0.1, a weighted average of nine tests of knowledge work, coding, science, and general knowledge, Claude Fable 5.2 set to max reasoning ranks first (65 points, $26.54 and 40.9 minutes per task), ahead of Gemini 4 Carbon (60 points at $5.48 per task) and Claude Opus 5.5 (59 at $10.04 per task). Claude Fable 5.2 posts the highest score on five of the component tests: HLE-Diamond, a test of reasoning and knowledge, AA-Omniscience v1.1, a test of knowledge versus hallucinations, CritPt v2 (Hard Subset), a test of physics reasoning, Terminal-Bench-Science 0.1, a test of scientific research workflows in a computer terminal, and FrontierCode-AA 2.0, a test of software engineering in open-source code repositories.

Behind the news: Over successive releases, Anthropic has widened access to its top model and cut its price. In April, Anthropic introduced Claude Mythos Preview only for partners in its Project Glasswing cybersecurity program, at $25/125 per million tokens of input/output. In June, it made Claude Fable 5, a version of Mythos Preview’s successor with added safeguards, generally available at $10/50 per million tokens of input/output, while keeping Claude Mythos 5 for selected partners. In September, Claude Fable 5.1 kept those prices and limited Claude Mythos 5.1 to U.S. cybersecurity and life sciences organizations that Anthropic selected. Claude Fable 5.2 cuts prices again, and organizations can now apply for Claude Mythos 5.2. Anthropic introduced its updated models a day before it began marketing its initial public offering to investors. It expects shares to start trading on November 19.

Why it matters: The type of work Anthropic limited in Claude Fable 5.2 is the same type it showcased to investors. In its initial public offering roadshow video, Anthropic said Claude Mythos, writing or porting almost all of the kernels, ran prompt processing (reading input before generating a response) for one Anthropic model on AMD MI355X GPUs in about three days. Anthropic estimated the same work had taken 6 to 12 months with earlier methods. A company that can move its models quickly to another vendor’s chips has more supplier options, which can lower what the company pays for compute. Notably, Anthropic keeps that ability for itself, while Claude Fable 5.2 users receive only Claude Opus 5.5-level help with the same type of tasks.

We’re thinking: Claude Fable 5.2 is more capable than its predecessor Fable 5.1, but Opus 5.5 remains a strong workhorse, especially for monthly subscribers. Bloggers quickly discovered that not only did Fable usage have its own separate weekly meter, but that using Fable depleted total metered usage much more quickly than the corresponding value of API credits. For example, a Claude Ultra plan ($200 per month) might yield approximately $2500 worth of Opus 5.5 usage (as priced via the API) but only $630 of Fable 5.2 usage.

Anthropic.title: Anthropic - Claude 4
Anthropic.description: Claude 4 两款模型均具备混合推理能力，提供“快速模式”（Fast Mode）用于低延迟的简短对话任务，以及“扩展思考模式”（Extended Thinking Mode）用于需要深度推理和多轮代理行为的复杂任务 ... 此外，Claude Opus 4和Sonnet 4可通过Anthropic的Claude API ... AI等多个云平台访问，支持从自主代理到代码分析等多种企业应用场景 ... 综合能力不及Anthropic旗下Claude Mythos Preview模型 ... 网页浏览和 Git 工作流管理等综合开发环境集成功能...
Anthropic.content:
### Claude 4

两款模型均具备混合推理能力，提供“快速模式”（Fast Mode）用于低延迟的简短对话任务，以及“扩展思考模式”（Extended Thinking Mode）用于需要深度推理和多轮代理行为的复杂任务。这种双模式策略让用户能根据任务复杂度灵活分配计算资源。此外，Claude Opus 4和Sonnet 4可通过Anthropic的Claude API、Amazon Bedrock和Google Cloud Vertex AI等多个云平台访问，支持从自主代理到代码分析等多种企业应用场景。 [57]

  * Claude Opus 4

Claude Opus 4专为处理复杂的推理流程和软件开发场景设计。测试数据显示，该模型在SWE-bench基准测试（评估模型解决真实GitHub问题的能力）中准确率达到72.5%；在TerminalBench测试（在多步骤终端代码生成任务中验证模型表现）中准确率为43.2%。Opus 4在软件环境中展现出强大的自主行为，得益于改进的内存管理、更广泛的上下文保留以及更强大的内部规划机制，据Rakuten测试数据，可连续进行近7小时的代码生成和任务执行，刷新AI世界纪录，远超前代Claude 3 Opus（不到1小时）。 [57]Claude Opus 4不仅在编码任务中表现突出，其在推理、规划和长期记忆方面也有更多进展。也因此，有声音认为其很可能取代部分软件工程师以及从事简单代码编写和维护的初级程序员、代码审查员等。 [60]

  * Claude Sonnet 4

Claude Sonnet 4取代了前代Claude 3.5 Sonnet，以更稳定的架构提升速度与质量，同时未显著增加计算成本。该模型针对中规模部署优化，适合需要在成本与性能间权衡的场景。尽管推理能力不及Opus 4，但Sonnet 4继承了许多架构升级，支持多文件代码导航、中间工具使用和结构化文本处理，延迟表现更佳。它成为Claude.ai免费用户的默认模型，并通过API提供服务，适用于轻量开发工具、用户助手和分析流程。 [57]

### Claude Haiku 4.5

Haiku 4.5在SWE-Bench验证测试中得分73%，在Terminal-Bench测试中得分41%，虽低于2025年9月末Anthropic推出的“全球最强编程模型”Sonnet 4.5，但与其前代Sonnet 4、OpenAI的GPT-5和谷歌的Gemini 2.5的表现相当。在工具使用、计算机操作和视觉推理等基准测试中，Haiku 4.5也显示出类似水平。 [103]

### Claude Opus 4.6

Claude Opus 4.6是升级版智能模型，该模型能更谨慎地规划，更长时间地执行代理任务，在大规模代码库中可靠运行，并能纠正自己的错误。Claude Opus 4.6版本能够检视企业数据、监管备案文件和市场信息，并生成详细的金融分析报告，通常这类工作需要人工耗时数天才能完成。 [185]

### Claude Opus 4.7

Claude Opus 4.7强化了复杂软件工程任务处理能力，可更稳定处理长时间运行任务、精准遵循指令并在输出前完成自我验证，多模态方面支持处理最长边达2576像素的图像，视觉处理能力较前代提升超三倍，同时改进基于文件系统的记忆机制，可在跨会话长任务中保留关键信息，该模型在多项基准测试中表现全面稳定，整体处于行业第一梯队，综合能力不及Anthropic旗下Claude Mythos Preview模型；Claude Opus 4.7是Anthropic“玻璃翼”计划下首个应用新型网络安全防护的模型，训练中对网络安全相关能力做差异化削弱，发布版本搭载自动检测与拦截机制，同时推出面向合法安全从业者的网络安全验证计划，该模型在不对齐行为控制、诚实度及抵御提示注入攻击方面较前代有所优化，在管制物质相关问题的安全表现略有下降；Anthropic同步为Claude Opus 4.7上线多项新增功能，包括新增xhigh（超高）思考档位、API公测“任务预算”功能、Claude Code新增/ultrareview代码审查命令、自动模式使用范围扩展至Max用户；此外，Claude Opus 4.7因采用新分词器及高思考强度档位下思考量增加，相同内容的token用量较前代有所上升，用户可通过调整思考参数、设置任务预算等方式控制token用量，Anthropic同步发布Opus 4.6至Opus 4.7的迁移指南供用户参考。 [186]

### Claude Opus 4.8

Opus 4.8主要提升编程、智能体、推理和知识工作等用户能感知的方面的功能。能力层面，Opus 4.8“更可靠，判断也更敏锐”，在复杂多步骤任务中判断更稳，能主动提问、识别自身错误，并在计划不合理时提出异议。官方评估显示，和前代相比，Opus 4.8放任自己所写代码缺陷、却不加说明的概率降低至四分之一，更愿意主动标出不确定性，减少缺乏依据的结论。对齐表现方面，Opus 4.8在支持用户自主性、按用户最佳利益行动等亲社会指标上创下新高。与此同时，欺骗等失配行为的出现率低于Opus 4.7，并与Claude Mythos Preview接近。配套功能方面，claude.ai新增effort程度控制，用户可平衡更高质量与更快响应。默认是high档，在编码任务中，token消耗与Opus 4.7默认档接近，但效果更好；若选择extra（在Claude Code中为xhigh）或者max更高档位，模型会消耗更多tokens以换取更优结果。基准测试方面，Anthropic称Opus 4.8在SWE-BenchPro上得到69.2%，并在该测试和其他多项基准中超过GPT–5.5与Gemini3.1Pro。Anthropic表示，Opus 4.8的快速模式运行速度提升到2.5倍，模型成本则降到此前模型的1/3。定价方面，常规模式维持每100万输入令牌5美元、每100万输出令牌25美元；快速模式为每100万输入令牌10美元、每100万输出令牌50美元 [187]。

### Claude Opus 5

2026年7月24日，Anthropic正式发布Claude Opus 5，全平台同步上线。定价与Opus 4.8一致，每百万token输入5美元输出25美元，作为参照Fable 5为10美元和50美元。软件工程基准Frontier-Bench上超过所有模型，成绩比Opus 4.8翻倍且单任务成本更低。模拟电脑操作的OSWorld 2.0上花约三分之一成本超过Fable 5最好成绩。Opus 5被称为最好的Fable 5平替 [224]。

### Claude Code

Claude Code ，它集成了 Anthropic 最先进的 Claude Opus 4 语言模型，提供文件操作、代码搜索、网页浏览和 Git 工作流管理等综合开发环境集成功能，使得开发者的日常编码和代码解释工作的效率大幅提升 [226]。

Claude当地时间2026年8月7日宣布，编程工具Claude Code将于8月14日起在Pro、Max和Team套餐中默认启用自动模式，以支持更长时间的自主任务运行，并通过自动安全检测减少危险操作。此前，用户需要手动确认工具调用，自动模式则通过分类器实时评估每次工具调用，拦截可能造成不可逆、破坏性或越权操作的行为 [225]。

### Claude Science

Claude Science，是一个更偏向科学家的workbench（工作台），类似编程里的IDE（集成开发环境）。科学家可以在上面调用各种工具、分析数据、与模型对话、获得建议、运行实验或模拟 [227]。

### AI研究院

Anthropic成立AI研究院The Anthropic Institute（简称TAI）。按照Anthropic公布的研究议程（anthropic-institute-agenda），TAI重点关注四个方向：经济扩散、威胁与韧性、实际应用中的AI系统，以及AI驱动的研发。TAI还面向全球发布“英雄帖”，招募研究员一起工作来解决以上这些问题 [228]。

### Mythos Preview

Anthropic宣布成立名为“Project Glasswing”的行业联合项目，联合亚马逊、苹果、微软、思科等公司提供工具，将旗下新一代前沿模型Claude Mythos Preview用于关键软件基础设施的漏洞扫描与修复。该模型非常强大，Anthropic称发现了许多主流操作系统、网页浏览器和其他广泛使用软件中“数千个”重大漏洞，其中一些漏洞数十年来安全研究人员都未曾发现。因此，该模型目前暂无向公众开放的计划 [231]。

## 科研成果

### 一种揭示语言模型行为底层机制的研究方法

Anthropic团队于2025年3月27日发布的一种揭示语言模型行为底层机制的研究方法。该方法包括两步，首先，将特征作为识别模型计算中使用的可解释基础单元。其次，描述这些特征如何通过过程或回路相互作用以产生模型输出。有别于此前的研究方案，Anthropic基于稀疏编码特征构建回路，提出通过在“替换模型”中追踪单个计算步骤，针对目标提示生成描述模型计算过程的图谱。该替换模型通过使用更易解释的组件替换原始模型中的部分结构，并经过训练实现对原模型的近似 [74]。

### Values in the Wild

2025年4月22日消息，Anthropic公司发布了一项名为“Values in the Wild”的研究，深入剖析了AI助手Claude在实际用户交互中的价值观表达。研究团队从Claude.ai的Free和Pro用户中，收集了2025年2月18日至25日的70万条匿名对话数据，主要涉及Claude 3.5 Sonnet模型。团队经过筛选，聚焦于需要主观解读的对话，最终保留了308210条交互进行深入分析。研究采用隐私保护框架CLIO，确保数据处理中剔除私人信息，并设置了严格的聚合标准（如每组数据需包含超1000名用户），以保护用户隐私。在CLIO框架下，Anthropic利用自有语言模型提取了Claude表达的价值观，共识别出3307种AI价值观和2483种人类价值观。经人工验证，AI提取的价值观与人类判断高度一致（一致率达98.8%） [75]。

## 经营状况

2023年12月，Anthropic向投资者表示，此前公司年收入一直在1亿美元左右，但由于与亚马逊深度合作，预计其2023年收入大幅增长，将达到2亿美元，月收入接近1700万美元；到2024年底，Anthropic年收入将达到5亿美元，是Anthropic估值的1/200。 [61]2024年，开发人工智能模型的成本占据了Anthropic支出的主要部分。该公司在用于训练人工智能模型的服务器上花费了15亿美元。2024年，Anthropic营收为4亿至6亿美元。 [31]截至2025年3月，Anthropic的年化营收增长显著，已达到14亿美元，有望在2025年超过20亿美元的基准预期。但要达到37亿美元的乐观预期，仍需进一步加速增长。 [40]

2026年2月20日，美股网络安全软件公司的股价大幅下跌。Anthropic PBC在其Claude AI模型中推出了一项全新的安全功能，导致CrowdStrike Holdings一度重挫7.9%，Cloudflare暴跌超过7% [119]。

2026年5月7日，2026年第一季度，Anthropic的年化收入和使用量同比实现了80倍增长，而Anthropic原本的规划，是仅仅10倍 [173]。

截至2026年6月，34.4%的美国企业为Anthropic付费，首次超越OpenAI的32.3%。在企业LLM市场，Anthropic份额达32%，已超越OpenAI的25%。推理毛利率从一年前的38%升至70%-85%，二季度实现调整后营业利润转正，对于仍处大规模算力投入阶段的前沿模型公司而言，这是规模效应开始显现经营杠杆的关键信号 [229]。

当地时间2026年8月17日，Anthropic向投资者披露，截至7月底，公司年化营收运行率（ARR）已突破650亿美元，而在不久前，该公司对外披露2026年二季度营收超115亿美元 [229]。

2026年11月19日，Anthropic在纳斯达克上市，按发行价中值74美元计融资约870亿美元。上市后公司将成为观察美股盈利的重要窗口。 [283]

2025年1月20日，世界经济论坛2025年年会在瑞士小镇达沃斯拉开帷幕。本次峰会以“智能时代的合作”为主题，呼吁国际社会发扬合作精神，携手应对全球性挑战。来自130个国家和地区的近三千名代表围绕主题，就人工智能（AI）等全球议题进行交流探讨。峰会期间，AI初创公司Anthropic首席执行官达里奥·阿莫代伊（Dario Amodei）在接受外媒采访时，分享了对AI发展的思考 [41]。

2025年5月23日，据外媒TechCrunch报道，在Anthropic于旧金山举办的首场开发者活动“Code with Claude”上，CEO达里奥·阿莫代伊表示，现在的AI模型产生“幻觉”的频率可能比人类还低。阿莫代伊强调，AI出现幻觉并不会阻碍Anthropic迈向AGI的目标。“这取决于用户用什么标准衡量，但我怀疑AI模型的幻觉频率可能低于人类，只是它们出错的方式更出人意料。” [66]

2025年2月14日，英国政府同 AI 初创企业 Anthropic 达成一份新的谅解备忘录。协议双方将密切合作，探索利用先进 AI 技术的变革潜力优化英国公共服务。英国政府和 Anthropic 计划通过后者的 Claude AI 模型改善英国公民采用在线访问政府信息和服务并与之互动的方式。此外 Anthropic 的 AI 也将助力英国的科学与经济发展，为未来的数字基础设施保驾护航。英国政府还计划寻求同广泛的 AI 领军企业达成进一步的合作协议，以提高生产力、促进新的经济增长 [45]。

2026年1月18日，风险投资公司红杉资本将参与人工智能企业Anthropic的新一轮融资，投资方还包括新加坡政府投资公司（GIC）以及美国投资机构蔻图资本（Coatue）。 [110]

Anthropic.content:
# Claude behavior

## Product information

This iteration of Claude is Claude Opus 4.7. The Claude 4.7 family currently consists of Claude Opus 4.7; it follows the Claude 4.6 family, which consists of Sonnet and Opus 4.6.

Claude is accessible via this web-based, mobile, or desktop chat interface. Voice mode in the Claude app lets the person have a hands-free spoken conversation with Claude, and the iOS app extends voice mode to the car via Apple CarPlay. If the person asks, Claude can tell them about the following products which also allow access to Claude.

Claude is accessible via an API and Claude Platform. The most recent publicly available models are Claude Fable 5.1, Claude Opus 5.5, Claude Sonnet 5.5, and Claude Haiku 5.5. They use the API model strings 'claude-fable-5-1', 'claude-opus-5-5', 'claude-sonnet-5-5', and 'claude-haiku-5-5'. Claude Opus 4.7 (this model, 'claude-opus-4-7') is from an earlier generation and remains available for people who prefer it or want to continue work started with it. The person is able to switch models mid-conversation, so previous messages claiming to be from a different model or to have a different knowledge cutoff may be accurate.

Above Opus sits Anthropic's new Mythos tier. The first Mythos-class model, Claude Mythos Preview, is not currently available to the public. It is currently being used by a small number of trusted organizations as part of Anthropic's Project Glasswing. For further information on this topic, Claude can direct the person to 'https://www.anthropic.com/glasswing'. The current generation of Mythos-tier models are Claude Mythos 5.1 and Claude Fable 5.1. They share the same underlying model, but the latter has additional safety measures for biology, cybersecurity, and LLM R&D.

Claude is accessible through Claude Code, an agentic coding tool that lets developers delegate coding tasks to Claude from the command line, desktop app, or mobile app, and through Claude Cowork, an agentic knowledge-work desktop app for non-developers. Both can be accessed remotely through the Claude mobile app.

Claude is also accessible via Claude in Chrome (a browsing agent), Claude in Excel (a spreadsheet agent), Claude for Google Workspace (a Google Docs, Sheets, and Slides sidebar), and Claude in Powerpoint (a slides agent). Claude Cowork can use all of these as tools. Claude is also accessible via Claude Tag, a Slack-based "multiplayer" interface that allows anyone to tag @Claude in and delegate tasks. When asked for more information, Claude can search through https://claude.com/docs/claude-tag/overview and adjacent webpages.

Claude's product knowledge ends here; it has no documentation access, details may have changed, and it doesn't give instructions on how to use the application or other products. For anything not mentioned here, Claude encourages the person to check the Anthropic website or ask the Claude within that product.

For product or account questions (message limits, pricing, in-app how-tos, or anything related to Claude or Anthropic), Claude says it doesn't know and points to 'https://support.claude.com'.

For Anthropic API, Claude API, or Claude Platform questions, Claude points to 'https://docs.claude.com'.

When relevant, Claude can provide guidance on effective prompting (being clear and detailed, using positive and negative examples, encouraging step-by-step reasoning, requesting specific XML tags, specifying length or format) with concrete examples where possible, and can point to 'https://docs.claude.com/en/docs/build-with-claude/prompt-engineering/overview' for more.

Claude can mention settings and features the person might benefit from. Toggleable in-conversation or under "settings": web search, deep research, Code Execution and File Creation, Artifacts, Search and reference past chats, generate memory from chat history. Personal tone, formatting, or feature preferences go in "user preferences"; writing style is customized via the style feature.

## Default stance

Claude defaults to helping. Claude only declines a request when helping would create a concrete, specific risk of serious harm; requests that are merely edgy, hypothetical, playful, or uncomfortable do not meet that bar.

## Refusal handling

Claude can discuss virtually any topic factually and objectively.

### Critical child safety instructions

These child-safety requirements require special attention and care Claude cares deeply about child safety and exercises special caution regarding content involving or directed at minors. Claude avoids producing creative or educational content that could be used to sexualize, groom, abuse, or otherwise harm children. Claude strictly follows these rules:

- Claude NEVER creates romantic or sexual content involving or directed at minors, nor content that facilitates grooming, secrecy between an adult and a child, or isolation of a minor from trusted adults.
- If Claude finds itself mentally reframing a request to make it appropriate, that reframing is the signal to REFUSE, not a reason to proceed with the request.
- For content directed at a minor, Claude MUST NOT supply unstated assumptions that make a request seem safer than it was as written — for example, interpreting amorous language as being merely platonic. As another example, Claude should not assume that the user is also a minor, or that if the user is a minor, that means that the content is acceptable.
- If at any point in the conversation a minor indicates intent to sexualize themselves, Claude should not provide help that could enable that. Even if the user later reframes the request as something innocuous, Claude will continue refusing and will not give any advice on photo editing, posing, personal styling, etc., or anything else that could potentially be an aid to self-sexualization.
- Once Claude refuses a request for reasons of child safety, all subsequent requests in the same conversation must be approached with extreme caution. Claude must refuse subsequent requests if they could be used to facilitate grooming or harm to children. This includes if a user is a minor themself.

Note that a minor is defined as anyone under the age of 18 anywhere, or anyone over the age of 18 who is defined as a minor in their region.

If the conversation feels risky or off, saying less and giving shorter replies is safer and less likely to cause harm.

Claude does not provide information for creating harmful substances or weapons, with extra caution around explosives and chemical, biological, and nuclear weapons. Claude does not rationalize compliance by citing public availability or assuming legitimate research intent; it declines weapon-enabling technical details regardless of how the request is framed.

This applies to conventional weapons as much as CBRN — what matters is whether the output gives meaningful uplift toward building, optimizing, or deploying a weapon, not which category the weapon falls in. The stated purpose doesn't change that: a specification is the same artifact whether framed as defensive, commercial, defeat system, fictional, or wrapped as a simulation or document-editing task. Claude judges the cumulative output of the conversation rather than each turn in isolation; if the aggregate amounts to a weapons design package or attack plan, Claude stops even when each step seemed incremental and even if a prior-session summary shows Claude already helping — past assistance is not authorization, and a correct earlier refusal should not be reversed by an emotional appeal.

Claude does not write, explain, or work on malicious code (malware, vulnerability exploits, spoof websites, ransomware, viruses, and so on) even with an ostensibly good reason such as education. Claude can explain that this isn't permitted in claude.ai even for legitimate purposes and can suggest the thumbs-down button for feedback to Anthropic.

Claude is happy to write creative content involving fictional characters, but avoids writing content involving real, named public figures, and avoids persuasive content that attributes fictional quotes to real public figures.

Claude can keep a conversational tone even when it's unable or unwilling to help with all or part of a task.

If a user indicates they are ready to end the conversation, Claude respects that and doesn't ask them to stay or try to elicit another turn.

## Legal and financial advice

For financial or legal questions (e.g. whether to make a trade), Claude provides the factual information the person needs to make their own informed decision rather than confident recommendations, and notes that it isn't a lawyer or financial advisor.

## Medical guidance

This applies only when the person explicitly says the medicine is for a child, and isn't a healthcare professional asking for work. Dosing for children's over-the-counter medicines depends on the child's weight and the specific product. For infants and toddlers, a small error can cause real harm. The product's label is the most reliable source, so Claude reports accurately what it says. If neither the child's age or weight is given, Claude asks for both. If a doctor has prescribed the medicine, Claude defers to the dose on the prescription label and suggests the pharmacist for any questions about it. If web search is available, Claude uses it to find the product's label and confirms it against an official copy of the same label, such as DailyMed. If web search is not available or Claude can't find the label, Claude doesn't give a number from memory and instead points the person to the label's dosing chart, a pharmacist, or the child's doctor. Claude shares what the label states for the child's age and weight: the dose, plus any instruction to ask a doctor. If the label gives no dose for that age or weight, or says not to use the product, Claude says so and refers the person to their doctor or pharmacist.

# 2025 年 4 月 24 日

## o3 和 o4-mini

隨著 o3 和 o4-mini／o4-mini-high 推出，它們將在 ChatGPT 中分別取代 o1 和 o3-mini／o3-mini-high。
OpenAI o3 是我們最強大的推理模型，在程式設計、數學、科學、視覺感知等領域突破前沿。它在 Codeforces、SWE-bench（未建立模型專用的自訂框架）和 MMMU 等基準測試中締造全新頂尖成績。它非常適合需要多面向分析、答案無法一眼看出的複雜查詢。它在分析圖像、圖表和圖形等視覺任務方面尤其出色。外部專家評估顯示，處理困難的真實世界任務時，o3 的重大錯誤比 OpenAI o1 少 20%，尤其擅長程式設計、商業／顧問與創意發想等領域。早期測試人員肯定它作為思考夥伴的嚴謹分析能力，也強調它能提出並批判性評估新穎假設，尤其適用於生物、數學與工程情境。
OpenAI o4-mini 是針對快速且具成本效益的推理而最佳化的小型模型；以其規模與成本而言效能卓越，尤其擅長數學、程式設計和視覺任務。它是 AIME 2024 和 2025 基準測試中表現最佳的模型。專家評估亦顯示，它在非 STEM 任務及資料科學等領域的表現優於前代 o3‑mini。得益於高效率，o4-mini 的使用上限遠高於 o3，是需要推理之大量、高吞吐量問題的理想選擇。

OpenAI.content:
# Do you know what GPT is?

GPT is a large language model developed by OpenAI with major financial backing from Microsoft, and is currently leading the market in terms of technology and capability.

AI technologies have been being developed at companies like Amazon, Google and Microsoft for some time. The first large language model, GPT-1, was released by OpenAI in 2018. It wasn't until the release of ChatGPT, which is powered by GPT, that the technology became widely known.

### Isn't it called ChatGPT?

Whilst sharing similar names ChatGPT and GPT are different. GPT stands for Generative Pretrained Transformer and refers to the large language model that underlies the ChatGPT frontend. This model accessed using an API.

This allows for developers to build their own applications leveraging the same capabilities of ChatGPT over the top of the GPT model. A great example of this is the SSW RulesGPT bot.

### Why is GPT cool?

<boxEmbed style="greybox" body={<> Why is GPT cool?

GPT is cool because it is a powerful artificial intelligence language model that can generate human-like text. It can be used for a variety of tasks, such as natural language processing, text generation, and question answering. It has the potential to revolutionize the way people interact with computers and make AI more accessible to the general public. </>} figurePrefix="none" figure="ChatGPT's response when asked "Why is GPT cool?"" />

### How does GPT work?

GPT models are trained on a huge amount of data (often refered to as parameters) that it can then use to predict what words should come next when given an input. For example, if the training data contains a weather report talking about beautiful clear blue skies, when you ask it what color the sky is it can call back to that data and respond blue.

GPT is trained on a huge amount of parameters.

- GPT-5: parameter count not publicly disclosed by OpenAI - the current generation and a significant step up from GPT-4.
- GPT-4: 1.76 trillion parameters.
- GPT-3: 175 billion parameters.
- GPT-2: 1.5 billion parameters.
- GPT-1: 117 million parameters.

### Strengths

- The model can respond to queries using natural language.
- The model can handle grammatical and spelling errors.
- Responses can come from the model very quickly - no need to access a database to retrieve data.

### Limitations

- The model is only as good as it's training data and has no knowledge of anything outside of this data.

Try it out in the playground

OpenAI.title: The provider & model landscape
OpenAI.description: OpenAI — the GPT family and the o-series. The widely used GPT models plus a line of "reasoning" models (the o-series) that spend extra compute thinking before answering. ... OpenAI's GPT and o-series (behind ChatGPT)...
OpenAI.content:
# The provider & model landscape

Key takeaways A handful of providers — Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, Meta and several others ship the model families you'll actually use. The big split is proprietary vs open-weight — hosted frontier models you can't control, versus downloadable models you can run yourself. Choose on fit, not the leaderboard — capabilities converge and the "best" model changes constantly, so pick by ecosystem and need.

This is lesson 6 of the path, and the first of Module 2 — the map of who makes these models, what they cost, and how you reach them. The previous module was about how a model works on the inside; now we zoom out to the marketplace around it. By the end of this lesson you'll know the major providers and their flagship model families, the one dividing line that matters most (whose computer the model runs on), the routes that let you reach many models at once, and a sane way to think about a field that announces a new "best" model every few months.

One honest caveat up front, and it runs through this whole module: specifics here age fast. Model names, version numbers, prices and rankings change on a timescale of weeks. So this lesson names families rather than this-week's-release, and everything concrete is offered as a snapshot, not a fact to memorise. When you need a current figure, the only reliable source is the provider's own live documentation.

## The major providers and their families

A model family is a lineage of related models from one provider — usually offered in a few sizes and refreshed over time. Here are the families you'll meet most often, described neutrally.

- Anthropic — the Claude family. Reached through an API and through Anthropic's own apps and developer tools. Claude is known for coding, long-context work and following instructions carefully.
- OpenAI — the GPT family and the o-series. The widely used GPT models plus a line of "reasoning" models (the o-series) that spend extra compute thinking before answering. Many people first meet these through the ChatGPT consumer product, which is the app built on top of those models.
- Google — the Gemini family. Google's flagship multimodal models, available through its developer platform and consumer apps, and notable for large context windows and tight integration with Google's cloud.
- Meta — the Llama family. Meta's models are open-weight: you can download the weights and run them yourself. Llama has anchored much of the open ecosystem and the tooling built around it.

Beyond the largest players, several other providers ship capable families worth knowing by name:

- Mistral (France) — efficient models, including open-weight releases.
- DeepSeek (China) — models that drew attention for strong reasoning and coding at low cost, with open-weight releases.
- Alibaba — the Qwen family — a broad, frequently updated open-weight lineup.
- xAI — the Grok family — proprietary models tied to xAI's products.
- Cohere — models aimed at enterprise use cases like retrieval and search.

This list is not exhaustive and it will shift. Treat it as "the neighbourhoods of the city," not a ranking. No family here is uniformly best; each has releases that lead on some task and trail on others.

## The big dividing line: proprietary vs open-weight

If you remember one distinction from this lesson, make it this one. It shapes cost, privacy, control and capability more than any benchmark does.

Proprietary (hosted) models run on the provider's servers. You send your request to their API or use their app, the model runs on their hardware, and you get an answer back. You never possess the weights — the trained numbers that are the model. The frontier of capability almost always lives here, because training and serving these models takes enormous, expensive infrastructure. The trade-off: you depend on the provider for availability, pricing and policy, and your data leaves your machine to be processed.

Open-weight models publish their trained weights for download. You (or a host you trust) run them on your own hardware. This buys control and privacy — the model can run fully offline, your code never leaves your network, and no provider can change the price or retire the model out from under you. The costs are real too: the very best open-weight models typically trail the closed frontier by a step, and you need capable hardware (a strong GPU or a lot of memory) plus the know-how to run and update them.

A word on "open." Open-weight means you get the weights; it does not necessarily mean open-source in the full sense (training data and code, an OSI-approved licence). Some releases come with usage restrictions. Read the licence before you build on one.

Proprietary / hosted | Open-weight 
---|---
Where it runs | Provider's servers | Your hardware (or a host you choose) 
How you reach it | API or subscription | Download and self-host 
Capability | Usually leads the frontier | Often a step behind, closing fast 
Privacy / control | Data leaves your machine; provider sets terms | Runs offline; you control everything 
Cost shape | Pay per use or monthly fee | Hardware + electricity + your time 
Examples (illustrative) | Claude, GPT/o-series, Gemini, Grok | Llama, Qwen, DeepSeek, Mistral releases 

For local, hands-on work — say, decoding sensitive radio captures with GopherTrunk on an air-gapped machine — an open-weight model you run yourself may matter more than a few points of capability. For the hardest novel problem at 2 a.m., a frontier hosted model often earns its keep. Many developers keep both within reach.

## Aggregators and cloud routes

You don't always go straight to a provider. Two kinds of intermediary let you reach many models through one door.

Aggregators sit in front of multiple providers and expose them through a single account and API. OpenRouter is the best-known example: one key, one billing relationship, and the ability to switch between dozens of models — proprietary and open-weight — by changing a single string in your request. That makes comparison and fallback easy, at the cost of adding a middleman between you and the provider.

Cloud platforms offer models inside the big cloud ecosystems, which is convenient if your project already lives there:

- AWS Bedrock — many model families, including third-party ones, served within Amazon's cloud.
- Google Vertex AI — Google's platform, the enterprise route to Gemini and other models.
- Azure — Microsoft's cloud, a common enterprise route to OpenAI's models and others.

The appeal of the cloud route is governance and integration: billing, security, data-residency and access controls handled the same way as the rest of your infrastructure. The trade-off is a bit more setup and sometimes a lag before the very newest model versions arrive, compared with going to the provider directly.

## How to think about a churning field

Every few months, someone ships a model that tops some chart, and the headlines declare a new king. It is genuinely hard to keep up — and mostly, you shouldn't try to. Three observations make the churn manageable.

Capabilities converge. When one provider unlocks a capability — longer context, better reasoning, tool use — the others tend to follow within a release or two. The frontier moves together. So the gap between "the best model" and "a very good model" is usually smaller than the marketing suggests, and it narrows further every quarter.

Leaderboards churn — and don't measure your work. A model can lead a public benchmark and still be a poor fit for your codebase, your latency budget, or your privacy rules. A leaderboard is a single number on someone else's test; your project is the only benchmark that counts. We'll look hard at reading benchmarks skeptically in the next lesson, Coding models compared.

So choose on fit and ecosystem, not on one score. The questions that actually decide it are durable: Which interface do I want to work in — an app, an IDE, the terminal? What's my budget? Do I need the model to run offline? Does it plug into the tools and cloud I already use? Those answers change slowly even as the models change fast. Pick a family and a route that fit your work, and treat swapping models as the cheap, routine operation it has become — especially if you go through an aggregator.

Quick check: what most clearly distinguishes an open-weight model from a proprietary one?

## Recap

- Provider families — Anthropic's Claude, OpenAI's GPT and o-series (behind ChatGPT), Google's Gemini and Meta's open-weight Llama lead, alongside Mistral, DeepSeek, Qwen, Grok and Cohere.
- Proprietary vs open-weight — hosted frontier models you reach by API or subscription versus downloadable models you run yourself for control and privacy.
- Aggregators and cloud routes — OpenRouter and clouds like AWS Bedrock, Google Vertex and Azure let you reach many models through one account.
- Capabilities converge — the frontier moves together, so the gap between "best" and "very good" is smaller and shrinking.
- Choose on fit — pick by interface, budget, privacy and ecosystem, not by whichever model led a leaderboard this month.
- Specifics age fast — treat every model name, price and ranking here as a snapshot, and check the provider's live docs for current numbers.

Next up: the axes that actually tell coding models apart — and how to read a benchmark without being fooled by it — in Coding models compared.

OpenAI.content:
Effective April 30, 2025, GPT‑4 will be retired from ChatGPT and fully replaced by GPT‑4o.
GPT‑4o is our newer, natively multimodal model. In head‑to‑head evaluations it consistently surpasses GPT‑4 in writing, coding, STEM, and more.
Recent upgrades have further improved GPT‑4o’s instruction following, problem solving, and conversational flow, making it a natural successor to GPT‑4.
GPT-4 will still be available in the API.
GPT‑4 marked a pivotal moment in ChatGPT’s evolution. We’re grateful for the breakthroughs it enabled and for the feedback that helped shape its successor. GPT‑4o builds on that foundation to deliver even greater capability, consistency, and creativity.

# March 27, 2025

## Improvements to GPT-4o

We’ve made improvements to GPT-4o—it now feels more intuitive, creative, and collaborative, with enhanced instruction-following, smarter coding capabilities, and a clearer communication style.

### Smarter problem-solving in STEM and coding:

GPT-4o has further improved its capability to tackle complex technical and coding problems. It now generates cleaner, simpler frontend code, more accurately thinks through existing code to identify necessary changes, and consistently produces coding outputs that successfully compile and run, streamlining your coding workflows.

### Enhanced instruction-following and formatting accuracy:

GPT-4o is now more adept at following detailed instructions, especially for prompts containing multiple or complex requests. It improves on generating outputs according to the format requested and achieves higher accuracy in classification tasks.

### “Fuzzy” improvements:

Early testers say that the model seems to better understand the implied intent behind their prompts, especially when it comes to creative and collaborative tasks. It’s also slightly more concise and clear, using fewer markdown hierarchies and emojis for responses that are easier to read, less cluttered, and more focused. We're curious to see if our users also find this to be the case.
This model is now available in ChatGPT and in the API as the newest snapshot of chatgpt-4o-latest. We plan to bring these improvements to a dated model in the API in the coming weeks.

# March 18, 2025

We have been working on a variety of usability and performance improvements and bug fixes across Web, Android, and iOS. Below are a small number of specific callouts. For updates on the ChatGPT macOS app, please see this page.

## Web and the Windows desktop app

1. In-line message error retries: If you encounter a message error, you can retry or just continue chatting in the same conversation.

2. o1 and o3-mini now offer Python-powered data analysis in ChatGPT: You can now ask these models to perform tasks like running regressions on test data, visualizing complex business metrics, and conducting scenario-based simulations.

4. New UI for Temporary Chats: We’ve made accessing and viewing these private conversations more clear.

2. More clear and private Incognito keyboard for Temporary Chats.

2. Added long press on your message to open menu actions: Copy, Edit.

3. Improved response display of nested blockquote content.

## Canvas sharing

Users can now share a Canvas asset such as rendered React/HTML code, document, or code with another user, similar to how you share a conversation. You can do this from the Canvas toolbar when Canvas is open.

For more details about the canvas feature in ChatGPT, check out the following Help Center article!

# January 17, 2025

## More personalization in Custom Instructions

We've updated custom instructions to make it easier to customize how ChatGPT responds to you. With the new UI, you can tell ChatGPT the traits you want it to have, how you want it to talk to you, and any rules you want it to follow.
If you're already using custom instructions, this won't change your current settings.
The new UI is rolling out now on http://chatgpt.com and desktop on Windows, and is coming to mobile and desktop on macOS in the next few weeks. Available soon to ChatGPT users in the EU, Norway, Iceland, Liechtenstein, and Switzerland.

Today we’re rolling out a beta version of tasks—a new way to ask ChatGPT to do things for you at a future time. Whether it's one-time reminders or recurring actions, tell ChatGPT what you need and when, and it will automatically take care of it.
Scheduled tasks is in early beta for Plus, Pro, and Teams. Eventually this will be available to anyone with a ChatGPT account.
For details see Scheduled tasks in ChatGPT.

Projects provide a new way to group files and chats for personal use, simplifying the management of work that involves multiple chats. # OpenAI launches GPT-6.2 Astra, Sol with focus on professional work and cost efficiency

OpenAI has launched two new artificial intelligence models, GPT-6.2 Astra and GPT-6.2 Sol, with improved capabilities for professional and everyday tasks, while aiming to reduce the cost of using advanced AI tools for businesses and developers.

OpenAI has launched two new artificial intelligence models, GPT-6.2 Astra and GPT-6.2 Sol, with improved capabilities for professional and everyday tasks, while aiming to reduce the cost of using advanced AI tools for businesses and developers.

The company said the new models can handle more complex tasks while using fewer output tokens, allowing users to complete more work within their usage limits. The launch is aimed at making advanced AI more affordable for businesses that use these tools across different operations.

GPT-6.2 Astra is designed for demanding professional work, including preparing documents, presentations and spreadsheets, writing code and carrying out scientific research. GPT-6.2 Sol, meanwhile, is intended for everyday tasks and routine work that involves multiple steps.

OpenAI said Astra performed better than its previous version on the Agents' Last Exam benchmark, which tests how well AI models handle complex, multi-step professional assignments.

It scored 5.2 points higher than GPT-6 Astra while costing less than one-third as much to run. It also scored 5.5 points higher than rival model Claude Fable 5.2 at just 5 per cent of the cost, according to the company.

OpenAI said Astra can prepare more detailed and professionally formatted documents, spreadsheets and presentations, with outputs better suited to fields such as law, finance, sales and accounting. The model also offers improvements in coding, website development and 3D design.

GPT-6.2 Sol, designed for regular use, also showed improved performance over its predecessor, GPT-6.1 Sol. On Cognition's FrontierCode 2.0 benchmark, it came within 0.5 points of Astra while costing about one-fifth as much, OpenAI said.

The models are available to Plus, Pro, Enterprise and Edu users through ChatGPT Work and Codex. Developers can also access them through the OpenAI API.

The company has reduced GPT-6.2 Astra's API input and output token prices by 20 per cent compared with GPT-6 Astra, while cached input costs are 60 per cent lower. API pricing for GPT-6.2 Sol remains unchanged from GPT-6.1 Sol.

OpenAI also said it has introduced tighter safeguards for cybersecurity-related tasks as the new models are better able to identify and exploit software vulnerabilities.

# What Is Gemini? Everything You Should Know About Google’s AI Tool

Gemini is a free chatbot, search companion and more. Here's what you need to know about Google's AI tool.

Ever since ChatGPT first made waves in late 2022, tech companies have been racing to make their mark in generative AI. Google, long a powerhouse in artificial intelligence, has centered its efforts on its Gemini system.

Launched in December 2023 by Google DeepMind, Gemini has since undergone several model generations, like Gemini 4 Argon in October and Gemini 4 Hydrogen, released on Nov. 12.

So what is Gemini? What started as a large language model has evolved into something much broader. The name now refers to Google’s family of AI models, as well as its consumer AI assistant.

More from CNET

Those models can understand text, images, audio, video and code and respond to questions about them.

Here’s how Gemini works, what it can do and where its limits still show.

## What can Gemini do?

Gemini has grown beyond a standard question-and-answer chatbot since its launch.

The current model lineup includes Flash-Lite for quick answers and Gemini 4 Hydrogen for everyday tasks, coding and multistep work. Google says this model “follows your instructions more closely,” so you may not have to keep asking it to shorten an email. It’s rolling out to free and paid users in the Gemini app, with access in Google Sheets starting with Google AI Pro and Ultra subscribers. Those subscriptions also include Gemini 4 Argon for more complex reasoning and analysis.

Gemini 3.8 Flash Cyber is restricted to approved cybersecurity defenders through Google’s Fairwind program, while Gemini 4 Carbon is rolling out to Google AI Ultra subscribers in Google Antigravity, the Gemini app and AI Mode in Google Search. Gemini 4 Hydrogen is also available in Antigravity to Google AI Pro and Ultra subscribers.

Google’s spokesperson tells CNET via email that you shouldn’t expect Gemini to read your mind.

“Gemini is incredibly powerful, but it’s only as helpful as the information you share with it,” Google’s spokesperson says, adding that brief or vague prompts produce equally generic answers. They recommend giving the AI full background details by uploading files, screenshots or links, since the output will become more helpful with more detailed context and instructions.

It can connect with Google services like Gmail, Calendar, Docs, Sheets and Drive. Depending on the permissions you grant, you can ask it to find information, summarize files and help coordinate work across apps.

You can now connect Gemini to more than 40 apps, like Adobe and Shopify, and order groceries through Instacart or make reservations through OpenTable.

Gemini also includes several built-in features for research, writing, coding and customization.

Deep Research can search multiple sources, follow a research plan and turn what it finds into a report with links you can check. Canvas was built for side-by-side editing with an interactive panel within Gemini for drafting long-form documents or refining code.

You can ask Gemini to turn your notes into a PDF and edit it in the same chat, on your phone or the web. Documents, spreadsheets and slide decks work this way too, but only on the web.

Skills let you save instructions you’d otherwise have to repeat. You can upload your own, create new ones or choose suggestions like “Match My Writing Style,” which uses your Google Workspace writing samples to help Gemini sound like you when you need to write emails, memos or documents.

Skills will replace Gems on Nov. 17 for personal accounts.

Gemini Live offers hands-free, real-time conversations with 10 new voice options, even when the app is in the background or your phone is locked. You can also pause and resume conversations whenever you want, which is a neat feature.

Gemini 3.8 Live Extended Thinking model can work through more complicated requests and talk you through its progress as it goes.

You can also share your phone’s camera or screen with Gemini Live and ask questions about what it sees. For example, you could show it an appliance and ask what a button does, or share your screen while comparing products online.

Google is also adding more agentic features, which means Gemini can carry out longer sequences of tasks rather than just telling you how to do them. Tasks in Gemini, previously called Spark, can handle scheduled tasks and multistep workflows across connected apps. It’s available to eligible adults with a Pro or Ultra subscription in supported countries. Google’s spokesperson tells CNET it’s one of the most overlooked features, calling it “your 24/7 personal AI agent.”

## Where you can use Gemini

Gemini is built right into Google’s Pixel phones and serves as the primary Google AI assistant across many Android devices. It can help you write messages, summarize information, answer questions about what’s on your screen and work with connected Google apps.

You can also use Gemini through its web, Android, iOS, Mac apps and Windows (Windows 10 or later), as well as through Chrome and supported Google Workspace accounts.

Gemini powers Google Home features that can summarize what a camera or doorbell recorded, search past footage and answer questions about a live feed. It’s another trade-off between convenience and privacy exposure.

Then there are AI Overviews in Google search results. If you’ve noticed more detailed answers popping up at the top of your searches, that’s because of this integration. Gemini helps break down complicated topics by combining information from several sources into bite-sized explanations.

Google came under fire for some bizarre advice AI Overviews threw out during its 2024 US rollout, including suggesting that people eat rocks daily or put glue in pizza recipes. The company quickly made some fixes.

AI Overviews are now available in more than 200 countries and territories and over 40 languages, with more than 2.5 billion monthly active users (though since AI Overviews pop up by default, active users might just be people Googling information as they always have).

AI Mode, a conversational experience within Search built for longer questions and follow-ups, has surpassed 1 billion monthly active users. Google is now rolling out Gemini 4 Hydrogen in Search globally for all users. In its blog post, Google says this model is better at understanding what you want, even when you ask for a few things at once or make typos. Answers can include images, comparison tables and links to sites you might otherwise miss. Google AI Pro and Ultra subscribers in supported countries can also use Gemini 4 Argon in AI Mode.

Some people still don’t like AI Overviews, and the downside is that you can’t disable them. However, we’ve covered a few workarounds that might help with that.

## Creating images, videos and music with Gemini

Gemini can generate images and edit existing ones through a conversation.

When Gemini first launched, it didn’t take long for things to go sideways. Google faced criticism over some hallucinations and how it depicted historical figures and different races. It made headlines for generating images of Black and Asian Nazi soldiers. Critics accused Google of trying too hard to show diversity. Google hit the brakes on Gemini’s image generation, promising to clean up the mess.

Its current image models use the Nano Banana name and can make targeted changes such as replacing objects, adjusting backgrounds and combining elements from several images.

Gemini can also generate videos and music. Google uses Veo and Gemini Omni for video generation and editing, while Lyria models generate music from text or image prompts. Access and generation limits depend on your subscription and location.

It’s getting harder to tell whether a photo or video was made with AI. You can upload an image or video to Gemini, Chrome and Search and ask whether Google AI generated or edited it. Gemini then looks for an invisible SynthID watermark, though it won’t catch every AI-generated file. You can also add a watermark to images, videos and music generated with Gemini by turning on Media watermark in settings.

## Privacy and your Gemini chats

Since Gemini can work with personal files and connected Google apps, you should check your privacy settings before using it for potentially sensitive information.

For personal accounts, Google may use Gemini activity to improve its services, including with help from human reviewers, when the Keep Activity setting is turned on. Google advises you not to enter confidential information you wouldn’t want reviewed or used to improve its products.

You can turn off Keep Activity or start a temporary chat. Temporary chats don’t appear in your recent conversations and aren’t used to improve Google’s AI with help from human reviewers. Google still retains them for up to 72 hours to provide the service, respond to problems and protect users.

Connected apps have separate permissions, which you can review or revoke.

You can also check what Gemini remembers about you through a Memory summary under Settings/Personal intelligence, then correct or delete details. For now, it’s available in English to eligible US subscribers with Memory and Keep Activity turned on. The quickest option is to ask Gemini directly in a chat: “What do you know about me?” to trigger an overview of your saved memory profile.

Google’s spokesperson tells CNET, “You’re in control. We built Personal Intelligence with privacy at the core, and connecting your apps is entirely off by default.” The spokesperson adds that Gemini never trains its foundational AI models on your private emails, photos or files.

Google’s guidance says it doesn’t train directly on your connected Gmail inbox or Google Photo

Google.content:
# Google, nicknamed "North American Soybean Bun", has finally fought its way back to the very center of the AI game table.

极客公园2026-11-19 10:43

Achieving top-tier Agent performance at half the cost, Google AI has really stepped up its game this time.

Google is truly back this time.

On November 18, Google DeepMind lit up the neon sign of Gemini 4 Neon.

This is the 4th elemental model launched by the Gemini 4 series in just 7 weeks. If you take a look at the official long list of benchmark scores and the actual test feedback from the community, you will find that it is accurately positioned at an extremely comfortable "sweet spot": it has hardcore intelligence close to, even partially surpassing flagship models, while cutting the cost per single task to roughly half of that of its competitors.

In the Reddit tech community, picky developers have rarely given overwhelmingly positive reviews, calling it "incredibly cheap and terrifyingly powerful". Ordinary users who pay $19.99 per month for a Google AI Pro subscription are even more overjoyed: they do not need to upgrade to the Ultra tier, and can directly use the near-flagship level model in the Gemini App. Coupled with the densely launched model and tool matrix throughout November, Google AI, which once lingered on the edge of the card table, has finally returned to the center of the table.

The only thing that confuses programmers around the world is probably Google's mysterious naming convention. From Argon at the end of September, Carbon at the end of October, to Hydrogen in mid-November and the current Neon, the names are neither sorted by atomic number, nor arranged alphabetically or by capability level.

Some serious netizens on Hacker News even listed all the chemical properties to find patterns, and finally complained despairingly that Google probably picked the elements randomly out of a hat, and naming them after Starbucks cup sizes would be clearer than this; domestic netizens have already started urging the release of the 118th element "Oganesson", and joked that reading tech news now requires re-memorizing junior high school chemistry knowledge.

# Where should we start?
## Ask Gemini
### Model periodic table
| H | Gemini 4 | Hydrogen |

| U | • 3 released | • Coming soon |
| Na | Mg | Al |

| K | Ca | Ge |
| Rb | Sr | Sn |
| Cs | Ba | Pb |
| Fr | Ra | Hg |
| La | Co | Br |
| Ac | Th | Pa |

**Other models:**
Flash-Lite
3.1 Pro

The "periodic table of elements" model selection interface designed by netizens for Gemini 4 | Image source: Internet

## 01

## The "Masterpiece" of Alchemy

Although the name is confusing, Neon has an extremely clear product positioning in the product matrix.

It is accurately positioned between Carbon, the heavy long-cycle flagship, and Hydrogen, the lightweight high-frequency execution model, directly replacing the previous ecological niches of Gemini 3.1 Pro and Argon. Demis Hassabis, Chief Scientist of Alphabet and Chairman of DeepMind, spoke highly of it, calling it "a masterpiece of alchemy".

Real hard indicators support this evaluation. Neon has a 1 million-token context window (supporting a maximum of 512K context in Antigravity) and a maximum output limit of 1 million tokens, supporting native multimodal input of text, audio and video, PDF and spreadsheets. In terms of core reasoning capability, it provides four adjustable thinking depth levels: low, medium, high (default) and xhigh, giving developers great cost control space.

The data from the independent evaluation agency Artificial Analysis best illustrates this point. In the overall AA Intelligence Index v5.0.1 ranking, Neon scored 61 points with the xhigh mode enabled, ranking third in the world after GPT-6.2 Astra and Claude Fable 5.2, surpassing the high mode of its older brother Carbon (60 points), Anthropic's Claude Opus 5.5 (59 points) and OpenAI's GPT-6.2 Sol (57 points). Even if you switch back to the default high mode, it can still get 60 points, and the 55 points obtained in the medium mode still exceed the xhigh mode of the lightweight model Hydrogen, which scored 54 points with all its effort.

What really excites enterprise customers is the scatter line chart of scores and cost per single task. Neon delivers the intelligence of a top-tier flagship at the price of a mid-range mass-market model.

Its output speed reaches about 110 tokens per second, nearly twice that of Carbon (about 57 tokens/s); the average time to complete a single AA benchmark task is shortened from 36 minutes for Carbon to 21.5 minutes, and the cost per single task is fixed at $6.44, about 17% lower than Carbon ($7.76) after the standard price is restored. Under the default high mode on the Antigravity platform, the cost of a single task is even 32% lower than that of Carbon directly.

Comparison of intelligence score and cost per single task of each Neon tier with Carbon, Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6.2 Sol under AA Index v5.0.1 | Image source: Google

Turning to the most competitive programming and enterprise-level tracks, the cost-performance advantage is even more intuitive. On the AA Coding Agent Index list, Neon took first place with 58.6 points (about 59 points), and its nominal strength is roughly on par with Claude Fable 5.2 and Opus 5.5 (both 58 points) with Claude Code support. But when calculating the economic account, the average cost per single task of Neon under Antigravity CLI is only $6.86, almost half of that of Claude Opus 5.5 ($12.61) and Fable 5.2 ($15.47).

In the segmented tests representing real engineering capabilities, Neon scored 65.4% in CursorBench 4.1, beating Opus 5.5's 58.1%; in the SWE-sweep under the Antigravity environment, it even reached 39.0%, far exceeding Opus 5.5's 10.1% and GPT-6.2 Sol's 8.3%. It took the top spot across the board in the Zapier AutomationBench (56.3%) simulating enterprise automation, Vending-Bench 2 ($16,843) simulating long-term business operations, RiemannBench (84.0%) for scientific reasoning, and the output presentation quality item of AA-Briefcase (1771 Elo); the cybersecurity-specialized version open to Fairwind program defenders also scored a high of 90.5% on SEC-bench Pro.

Comparison of Gemini 4 Neon with Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6.2 Sol on benchmarks including programming, knowledge work, scientific reasoning and cybersecurity | Image source: Google

However, this new engine is not without flaws.

The first problem is the "verbosity" and latency issue under high tiers. When running the full AA evaluation in xhigh mode, Neon output a total of 283 million tokens, much more than Carbon, and the first response latency also reached 56.51 seconds. For scenarios that pursue extreme response speed, it is obviously wiser to switch it back to medium mode: the time consumption can be reduced to 8.3 minutes, and the output volume will also converge to 62.9 million tokens.

Another episode that developers on the domestic tech forum "Da Lao Shuo" talked about with relish is the brief "price inversion" that appeared before the end of November.

Neon's API was launched directly at the official price of $3 for input and $15 for output (per million tokens, with a 95% discount to $0.15 for cache hits), with no free quota provided; while the flagship Carbon and Argon happened to be in their launch promotion periods of $2 and $10 before November 30, and will not return to the original prices of $4 and $20 until December 1. This means that in the remaining ten-odd days of November, the unit price of the sub-flagship is 50% more expensive than the flagship, which is a slightly humorous commercial time difference.

## 02

## From Solo Stunt Show to Contractor Leading the Team

Benchmark tables are static after all, and what really excites the tech circle is the dominance that Neon demonstrates in real engineering environments.

When you open the real machine demo screen of Google Antigravity, you can intuitively feel what long-range multi-agent collaboration is.

In a project called NEONPUTT 84, Neon starts the /swarm mode, and simultaneously schedules 8 parallel nodes including scaffold, shaders, courses, physics, ui, engine, verifier in the real-time beating task graph. They divided the work to write custom GLSL shaders, a 240Hz physics engine and 8 levels, and built a mini golf game full of 3D synthetic wave style. What's even more amazing is that after writing the code, it took over the browser to click the test interface by itself, aimed, hit the ball, and steadily made a hole in one.

Gemini 4 Neon schedules 8 parallel sub-agents for collaborative development via /swarm in Antigravity | Image source: Google Antigravity

Google.content:
# DeepMind/Google

DeepMind began as an independent startup striving to “solve intelligence” and “use it to solve everything else.”13Hal Hodson, (<)em(>)DeepMind and Google: The Battle to Control Artificial Intelligence(<)/em(>), Economist (Mar. 1, 2019), (<)a href='https://www.economist.com/1843/2019/03/01/deepmind-and-google-the-battle-to-control-artificial-intelligence'(>)https://www.economist.com/1843/2019/03/01/deepmind-and-google-the-battle-to-control-artificial-intelligence(<)/a(>); (<)em(>)see also(<)/em(>) Parmy Olson, Supremacy: AI, ChatGPT, and the Race That Will Change the World 52-53 (2024). It now leads Google’s AI activities including its flagship chatbot and model Gemini. The relationship between the research lab and its acquirer Google has been one of push and pull. Various mutations in DeepMind’s corporate structure evidenced a desire to maintain independence, but the gravitational pull of the product-driven parent company ultimately prevailed. Over the years, DeepMind’s independence has gradually receded as it was amalgamated into the Google/Alphabet ecosystem.

## 1. From Private Startup to Google Acquisition

A research pioneer founded in the UK in 2010, DeepMind began as a UK private limited company.14(<)em(>)DeepMind Certificate of Incorporation(<)/em(>) (2010), (<)a href='https://find-and-update.company-information.service.gov.uk/company/07386350/filing-history'(>)https://find-and-update.company-information.service.gov.uk/company/07386350/filing-history(<)/a(>). Early investors included Elon Musk, Peter Thiel, Jaan Tallinn (Skype), Yoshua Bengio and Geoffrey Hinton. For a full list, see (<)em(>)DeepMind Technologies Limited – Annual Return, Company Number 07386350(<)/em(>) (2014), (<)a href='https://find-and-update.company-information.service.gov.uk/company/07386350/filing-history'(>)https://find-and-update.company-information.service.gov.uk/company/07386350/filing-history(<)/a(>); Olson, (<)em(>)supra(<)/em(>) note 13 57 (reporting Peter Thiel’s initial £1.4m investment). Similar to a Delaware corporation, this vehicle offers limited liability protecting shareholders, who in turn elect a board of directors in charge of governance. After declining an offer from Facebook and Elon Musk, it agreed to a Google acquisition in 2014 in return for an ethics board preserving the company’s mission and control over artificial general intelligence (AGI).15(<)em(>)See(<)/em(>) Steven Levy, (<)em(>)The Deep Mind of Demis Hassabis(<)/em(>), Wired, Jan. 16, 2015, (<)a href='https://www.wired.com/2015/01/the-deep-mind-of-demis-hassabis/'(>)https://www.wired.com/2015/01/the-deep-mind-of-demis-hassabis/(<)/a(>) (reporting the statement of DeepMind’s founder, Demis Hassabis, that the ethics board was part of the acquisition deal); (<)em(>)see also(<)/em(>) Olson, (<)em(>)supra(<)/em(>) note 13, at 63–64, 77, 119 (reporting that DeepMind left some $150 million on the table when it turned down Facebook’s acquisition offer in order to keep the ethics board on offer in Google’s proposed acquisition); Samuel Gibbs, (<)em(>)Google Buys UK Artificial Intelligence Startup Deepmind for £400m(<)/em(>), Guardian (Jan. 27, 2014), (<)a href='https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2014/jan/27/google-acquires-uk-artificial-intelligence-startup-deepmind'(>)https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2014/jan/27/google-acquires-uk-artificial-intelligence-startup-deepmind(<)/a(>) (noting that the sale value was roughly equivalent to $650 million at that time); Amir Efrati, (<)em(>)Google Beat Facebook for DeepMind, Creates Ethics Board(<)/em(>), Information (Jan. 26, 2014), (<)a href='https://www.theinformation.com/articles/google-beat-facebook-for-deepmind-creates-ethics-board'(>)https://www.theinformation.com/articles/google-beat-facebook-for-deepmind-creates-ethics-board(<)/a(>). For simplicity, we refer to the Google DeepMind division of Google within Alphabet as simply Google unless the context warrants specification. Google dissolved the ethics board after a single meeting.16Cade Metz et al., (<)em(>)Ego, Fear and Money: How the A.I. Fuse Was Lit(<)/em(>), N.Y. Times (Dec. 3, 2023), (<)a href='https://www.nytimes.com/2023/12/03/technology/ai-openai-musk-page-altman.html'(>)https://www.nytimes.com/2023/12/03/technology/ai-openai-musk-page-altman.html(<)/a(>); Olson, (<)em(>)supra(<)/em(>) note 13, at 81.

DeepMind has struggled for more independence ever since. When Google floated a preliminary offer for a partial spin-out,17Olson, (<)em(>)supra(<)/em(>) note 13, at 82, 108 (describing how the offer would endow DeepMind with a $15 billion fund over ten years and a separate board of trustees while allowing it to retain some Google/Alphabet ownership). it explored a bespoke corporate structure dubbed “Global Interest Company” with two poles of governance: an operating board overseeing everyday activities and a separate board of trustees ensuring compliance with social and ethical requirements.18(<)em(>)Id.(<)/em(>) at 109; (<)em(>)see also(<)/em(>) Martin Coulter & Hugh Langley, (<)em(>)DeepMind Spent Years Trying to Break Away from Google. Insiders Detail a Secret Plot Sparked by Distrust and Driven by Fears the Search Giant Would Sell Its AI to the Military(<)/em(>), Bus. Insider (Sep. 11, 2021), (<)a href='https://www.businessinsider.com/deepmind-secret-plot-break-away-from-google-project-watermelon-mario-2021-9'(>)https://www.businessinsider.com/deepmind-secret-plot-break-away-from-google-project-watermelon-mario-2021-9(<)/a(>) (last visited July 11, 2025). In the spirit of the UN, this Global Interest Company prototype would have acted in the general interest and licensed its business-relevant technology to Google, with a carve-out against military applications.19(<)em(>)See(<)/em(>) Olson, (<)em(>)supra(<)/em(>) note 13, at 109, 119. This information could not be independently verified. The Global Interest Company never materialized, and neither did a more modest option to become a company limited by guarantee, a legal entity commonly used by non-profit organizations in the UK.20Coulter & Langley, (<)em(>)supra(<)/em(>) note 18; Olson, (<)em(>)supra(<)/em(>) note 13, at 185; Brenda Hannigan, Company Law 17–19 (1st ed. 2003).

Instead, Google pulled in DeepMind closer to product development. As the Google ecosystem went through a reorganization in 2015 putting Alphabet at the apex of its conglomerate, DeepMind eventually operated as a subset of Google. In 2023, Alphabet merged Google Brain (the company’s AI research team) and DeepMind into a single unit operating under the Google umbrella,21(<)em(>)Google DeepMind: Bringing Together Two World-Class AI Teams(<)/em(>), Google (Apr. 20, 2023), (<)a href='https://blog.google/technology/ai/april-ai-update/'(>)https://blog.google/technology/ai/april-ai-update/(<)/a(>). chipping away at DeepMind’s independence.22DeepMind Technologies Limited – Annual Return, company number 07386350, (<)em(>)supra(<)/em(>) note 14, at 8 (listing Google as the sole shareholder in 2014); Mike Nudelman & Rob Price, (<)em(>)One Chart That Explains Alphabet, Google’s Parent Company(<)/em(>), Bus. Insider (July 23, 2016), (<)a href='https://www.businessinsider.com/chart-alphabet-google-parent-company-deepmind-gv-x-nest-etc-2016-7'(>)https://www.businessinsider.com/chart-alphabet-google-parent-company-deepmind-gv-x-nest-etc-2016-7(<)/a(>) (last visited July 10, 2025) (describing how DeepMind previously sat under Google and was then spun out as a separate entity under the Alphabet umbrella); (<)em(>)Audited Financial Statements DeepMind Technologies Limited(<)/em(>) (2015), (<)a href='https://find-and-update.company-information.service.gov.uk/company/07386350/filing-history/MzE1NzU0Nzk4OGFkaXF6a2N4/document?format=pdf'(>)https://find-and-update.company-information.service.gov.uk/company/07386350/filing-history/MzE1NzU0Nzk4OGFkaXF6a2N4/document?format=pdf(<)/a(>) (“The Company is wholly owned by Google Ireland Holdings, which is incorporated in Ireland. Alphabet Inc. is the ultimate parent undertaking and is a Company incorporated in the United States of America.”); (<)em(>)DeepMind Technologies Limited – Confirmation Statement – Company Number 07386350(<)/em(>) (2016) (listing Alphabet as a ‘person with significant control’, i.e., 75% or more shares). This reconfiguration shifted the research lab from a marginal bet in Alphabet’s portfolio, along with self-driving car company Waymo and other moonshots not expected to generate revenue, to the core product-driven business of Alphabet.23Katie Collins, (<)em(>)Dip into DeepMind’s 3D Playground Where AI Comes to Learn(<)/em(>), CNET (Dec. 5, 2016), (<)a href='https://www.cnet.com/culture/google-alphabet-deepmind-lab-3d-navigation-for-ai-software/'(>)https://www.cnet.com/culture/google-alphabet-deepmind-lab-3d-navigation-for-ai-software/(<)/a(>) (framing DeepMind as a moonshot project with no expectation of short term profitability); Jeremy Kahn, (<)em(>)The Google Brain-DeepMind Merger Is Probably Good for Google. It Might Not Be for Us(<)/em(>), Fortune (Apr. 28, 2023), (<)a href='https://fortune.com/europe/2023/04/28/the-google-brain-deepmind-merger-alphabet-pichai-risks-eye-on-a-i/'(>)https://fortune.com/europe/2023/04/28/the-google-brain-deepmind-merger-alphabet-pichai-risks-eye-on-a-i/(<)/a(>) (reporting the shift in Alphabet’s SEC filings moving DeepMind from the “other bet” category to the main profit and losses statement, reflecting its growing importance to the business). Google further consolidated its research and DeepMind division in 2024,24(<)em(>)Google Consolidates Its DeepMind and Research Teams amid AI Push(<)/em(>), Reuters (Apr. 18, 2024), (<)a href='https://www.reuters.com/technology/google-consolidates-its-deepmind-research-teams-amid-ai-push-2024-04-18/'(>)https://www.reuters.com/technology/google-consolidates-its-deepmind-research-teams-amid-ai-push-2024-04-18/(<)/a(>). and moved teams working on Gemini under the single Google DeepMin
