#### tongyi-intent-detect-v3

意图识别和槽位填充是对话系统中的基础任务。本模型实现了一个基于 API的意图（intent）和槽位参数（slots）联合预测。在一次模型输出中，同时完成多个指令API的返回和槽位参数的填充。返回的结果为标准json格式。

#### videoretalk

VideoRetalk是一个人物视频生成模型，可基于人物视频和人声音频，生成人物讲话口型与输入音频相匹配的新视频。

AnimateAnyone-Template是辅助AnimateAnyone的动作模板生成模型，可基于视频提取人物动作并制作模板。

千问VL-OCR（qwen-vl-ocr），即基于Qwen-VL训练的OCR识别大模型。通过统一模型的方式聚合多种图文识别、解析、处理类任务，提供强大的图文识别能力。本模型为2024年10月28日的快照版本。

#### qwen-coder-plus

千问系列代码及编程模型是专门用于编程和代码生成的语言模型，性能出色，效果突出。

LivePortrait-detect是辅助LivePortrait的图像检测模型，用于检测图片中的人物形象是否符合视频生成要求。

#### liveportrait

LivePortrait是一款视频生成模型，可基于人物图片生成轻量化的人物肖像动态视频。

#### emo-v1

EMO是一款视频生成模型，可基于人物图片生成高质量的人物肖像动态视频。

#### emo-detect-v1

EMO-Detect是辅助EMO的图像检测模型，用于检测图片中的人物形象是否符合视频生成要求。

#### qwen-max

千问2.5系列千亿级别超大规模语言模型，支持中文、英文等不同语言输入。随着模型的升级，qwen-max将滚动更新升级。如果希望使用固定版本，请使用历史快照版本。

#### qwen-math-turbo

千问系列数学模型是专门用于数学解题的语言模型，推理速度快，成本低。

#### qwen-math-plus-0919

#### qwen-math-plus-latest

千问系列数学模型是专门用于数学解题的语言模型，推理效果好，模型性能优秀本模型为2024年9月19日快照版本，预计维护到下个版本发布后一个月（待定）。

千问系列代码及编程模型是专门用于编程和代码生成的语言模型，推理速度快，成本低。

大模型声音复刻服务依托先进的大模型技术进行特征提取，无需训练过程就可以完成声音的复刻。仅需提供极短的音频，即可迅速生成高度相似且听感自然的定制声音。 大模型声音设计使用FunAudioGen-VD模型，支持通过文本Prompt描述，创造声音。无需受限任何音频质量，根据目标场景对音色、语气、语调、语速、情绪等各方面表现力的需求描述，即可生成高质量语音。高度还原专业配音演员的演出水准。

#### qwen-math-plus

#### qwen-math-plus-0816

千问数学模型具有强大的数学解题能力,擅长处理中英文数学题，包括方程、计算、证明等方向。

#### cosyvoice-clone-v1

声音复刻Cosyvoice大模型，依托先进的大模型技术进行特征提取，从而完成声音的复刻，且无需训练过程。仅需提供时长较短的音频，即可迅速生成高度相似且听感自然的定制声音。

#### paraformer-v2

Paraformer语音识别模型，支持多个语种的语音识别。可以通过language_hints参数选择语种获得更准确的识别效果，支持任意采样率。 支持的语言包括：中文（含粤语等各种方言）、英文、日语、韩语。可支持热词。

#### paraformer-realtime-v2

Paraformer实时语音识别模型，支持多个语种自由切换的视频直播、会议等实时场景的语音识别。可以通过language_hints参数选择语种获得更准确的识别效果。支持任意采样率。 支持的语言包括：中文（含粤语等各种方言）、英文、日语、韩语。 可支持热词。

#### image-instance-segmentation

人物实例分割运用了检测和分割技术，不仅能够在图像中识别出不同的对象，而且还能准确地画出每一个对象边界的像素级掩码（mask）。

#### image-erase-completion

图像擦除补全通过指定图像mask中要删除的人体、宠物、物品、文字、水印等图像区域，在保留背景的同时移除图像中的一个或多个人物、物体、文字等元素，此功能不支持输入prompt的消除。擦除补全技术结合了计算机视觉、AIGC inpainting等先进技术，可以在多种场景下应用，从而满足用户对隐私保护、内容创作和图像编辑等方面需求。

#### deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 是 V4.1-Flash 的迭代版本，通过基于自反馈的强化学习（RL）训练，在 Terminal-Bench 4.0、DeepSWE v1.1、ProgramBench 等多项基准上较上版显著提升，同时缩短任务运行时间与输出长度，在多个 Harness 下达到新的性能–费用帕累托最优。模型从零构建完整项目的能力进一步增强，可支持游戏开发、3D 建模等“许愿式”编程任务，延续上一版的 552B 总参数 MoE、原生多模态视觉理解、1M 上下文与 384K 最大输出。

#### qwen3.8-omni-flash

Qwen3.8-Omni-Flash 支持文本、图片、音频和视频输入及文本输出，支持思考与非思考模式、Function Calling、联网搜索和上下文缓存，适用于音视频理解、多模态分析和智能体应用。

GLM.content:
Nov 19, 2026

# Is GLM Free? Weights, Free Models and API Costs

Is GLM free? GLM weights are free to download and Z.ai's Flash models cost nothing on its API, but flagship GLM-5.x use is paid. See what's free per version.

"GLM is free" and "GLM costs $4.40 per million tokens" are both true, and they can both appear on the same search results page. The difference is which GLM you mean and how you plan to use it: downloading the model, calling an API, or using it inside a chat app or coding tool.

Is GLM free? Partly. The model weights are free: GLM-4.6 through GLM-5.2 and GLM-5.3-Flash are MIT-licensed, and GLM-5.3 uses a permissive custom license. Some hosted models are free too: Z.ai's API lists GLM-4.7-Flash, GLM-4.5-Flash and GLM-4.6V-Flash at no charge. The flagship models aren't free to use as a service: GLM-5.x usage on Z.ai's API is billed per token, and its Coding Plan starts at $18 a month.

This guide breaks that down version by version, so you can tell a genuinely free option from a trial that runs out. It's based on Z.ai's official pricing page, Coding Plan documentation, Hugging Face model cards and license files, all reviewed November 19, 2026. We did not test every provider's promotional offer. GLM5 publishes this guide and operates independently of Z.ai.

## Is GLM Free? The Answer by Version

Model | Weights free to download? | Free on Z.ai's API? | Z.ai API price (input / output per 1M tokens) 
---|---|---|---
GLM-5.3 | ✅ Custom GLM-5.3 license | ❌ | $1.40 / $4.40 
GLM-5.3-Flash | ✅ MIT | ❌ | $0.15 / $0.50 
GLM-5.2 | ✅ MIT | ❌ | $1.40 / $4.40 
GLM-5.1 | ✅ MIT | ❌ | $1.40 / $4.40 
GLM-5 | ✅ MIT | ❌ | $1.00 / $3.20 
GLM-4.7 | ✅ MIT | ❌ | $0.60 / $2.20 
GLM-4.7-Flash | ✅ MIT | ✅ Free | Free 
GLM-4.6 | ✅ MIT | ❌ | $0.60 / $2.20 
GLM-4.5-Flash | — | ✅ Free | Free 
GLM-4.6V-Flash (vision) | — | ✅ Free | Free 

Prices are from Z.ai's pricing page. License information comes from each model's official Hugging Face repository.

## Free Option 1: Download the Weights

Every recent flagship GLM model publishes its weights. GLM-4.6, 4.7, 5, 5.1 and 5.2 use the MIT license, which allows free commercial use, modification and redistribution with the license notice kept.

GLM-5.3 is the exception worth knowing about. Its weights ship under a custom GLM-5.3 license. It grants the same broad rights as MIT, with one added condition: a company running a "model as a service" business with more than $10 billion in revenue over 12 months must pass Z.ai's security review before commercial use. For nearly everyone that condition never applies, but it means GLM-5.3 isn't technically MIT.

The catch with free weights is hardware. Flagship GLM checkpoints are hundreds of billions of parameters. GLM-5.2's is roughly 753 billion. Running them takes multi-GPU servers, which are expensive to buy or rent. "Free to download" is not "free to run."

The practical exception is GLM-4.7-Flash. It's a 30B-total, 3B-active model, small enough for far more modest hardware and also MIT-licensed. If you want a GLM model on your own machine at no software cost, it's the realistic starting point.

## Free Option 2: Z.ai's Free API Models

Z.ai's pricing page lists three models as completely free on its API: input, cached input and output all at zero.

- GLM-4.7-Flash: the lightweight GLM-4.7 variant, with a 200K-token context per Z.ai's documentation.
- GLM-4.5-Flash: an older lightweight model.
- GLM-4.6V-Flash: a free vision model that accepts images.

These are good for prototypes, personal projects, learning the API and light production tasks. They aren't the flagships. Expect them to trail GLM-5.x on hard coding and long agent tasks.

## What Isn't Free: Flagship API Usage

GLM-5, 5.1, 5.2 and 5.3 are paid per token on Z.ai's API. A rough sense of scale at GLM-5.2/5.3 rates ($1.40 input, $4.40 output per million tokens):

Usage | Approximate cost 
---|---
A short chat exchange (2K tokens in, 1K out) | Under one cent 
A 100K-token document plus a 2K-token answer | About $0.15 
A full 1M-token prompt plus a 10K-token answer | About $1.44 

Cached input, which is billed at $0.26 per million on Z.ai, makes repeated long prompts much cheaper.

## What About the GLM Coding Plan?

Z.ai's GLM Coding Plan is a subscription for using GLM inside coding tools such as Claude Code, Cline and OpenCode. Z.ai's documentation says plans start at $18 per month, with higher Pro and Max tiers. It isn't free. Z.ai has offered trial cards, but treat those as time-limited.

One detail affects what you get: on the Coding Plan, requests for GLM-5.2 or 5.1 are routed to GLM-5.3, and GLM-4.7 requests are routed to GLM-5.3-Flash, per the Coding Plan overview.

## Free GLM in a Browser

If you just want to try GLM without hardware or an API key, browser chat is the simplest path. On GLM5, the free Chat default is GLM 5.3 Flash, and other GLM models can be selected with credits. Open GLM5 Chat to try it, and check the model selector to see which GLM version is answering.

## Free Answers for Specific Versions

- Is GLM 5 free? The weights are free under MIT. Z.ai's API charges $1.00 input and $3.20 output per million tokens. See what GLM-5 is.
- Is GLM 5.1 free? The weights are free under MIT. API use is $1.40/$4.40. See what GLM 5.1 is.
- Is GLM 5.2 free? The weights are free under MIT, and API use is paid. Our detailed GLM 5.2 guide covers trials and providers.
- Is GLM 5.3 free? The weights are free under the GLM-5.3 license. API use is $1.40/$4.40, and GLM-5.3-Flash is the cheaper tier at $0.15/$0.50.
- Is GLM 4.7 free? The weights are free. GLM-4.7 itself is paid on the API, but GLM-4.7-Flash is free. See what GLM 4.7 is.

## How to Pick the Right "Free" Option

Your goal | Best free (or near-free) path 
---|---
Try GLM today, no setup | Browser chat 
Build a prototype with an API | GLM-4.7-Flash on Z.ai's free tier 
Run GLM on your own computer | GLM-4.7-Flash weights 
Image input for free | GLM-4.6V-Flash on Z.ai's free tier 
Flagship quality for real work | Paid API usage, starting small with token caps 

Rule of thumb: use free tiers to find out whether GLM fits your task. Pay for a flagship only once a free model has clearly failed on your real prompts.

## Frequently Asked Questions

### Is GLM free to use?

Partly. The weights are free to download, and Z.ai's API offers GLM-4.7-Flash, GLM-4.5-Flash and GLM-4.6V-Flash for free. Flagship GLM-5.x models are paid per token.

### Is GLM open source?

The weights are open: MIT for GLM-4.6 through GLM-5.2, and a permissive custom license for GLM-5.3. See what GLM is for background.

### What is the best free GLM model?

GLM-4.7-Flash. It's free on Z.ai's API, MIT-licensed, and small enough (30B total, 3B active) to self-host on modest hardware.

### Is the GLM Coding Plan free?

No. Plans start at $18 per month, according to Z.ai.

### Can I use free GLM models commercially?

MIT-licensed weights allow commercial use with the license notice kept. For hosted free tiers, check Z.ai's terms for rate limits and usage conditions.

## The Bottom Line

GLM is free in two real ways: open weights you can download, and a handful of Flash models Z.ai serves at no charge. It isn't free in the way most people hope, because the flagship GLM-5.x models cost money to run, whether you pay per token, subscribe to a coding plan or buy the GPUs yourself.

The smart path is to start free and pay only when you need to: try GLM in your browser on GLM5, test GLM-4.7-Flash on Z.ai's free tier, and move to a flagship once your real tasks prove they need it.

## Sources

- Z.ai API pricing — free Flash models and per-token prices for every GLM version.
- GLM-5.3 license — custom license terms and the security-review condition.
- GLM-4.7-Flash official model card — 30B-A3B size and MIT license.
- GLM Coding Plan overview — plan pricing and model routing.

Reviewed November 19, 2026. Free tiers, prices and plan terms change often. Confirm them on Z.ai's official pages before you rely on them.

## Start Using GLM 5 Today

Try GLM 5 free — reasoning, coding, agents, and image generation in one platform.

GLM.content:
Nov 19, 2026

# What Is GLM-5? Z.ai's 744B Agentic Model Explained

What is GLM-5? Z.ai's February 2026 open-weight model: 744B parameters, 40B active, 200K context, MIT license. Specs, benchmarks, pricing and how it fits 5.x.

"GLM 5" gets used for three different things. Sometimes it means one specific model released in February 2026. Sometimes it means the whole 5.x line, including GLM-5.1, 5.2 and 5.3. And sometimes it's simply the name of a website. If you've read a spec sheet that contradicts another one, that's usually why.

What is GLM-5? It's the open-weight foundation model Z.ai (Zhipu AI) released in February 2026. It started the GLM-5 generation. It has 744 billion total parameters with 40 billion active per token, a 200K-token context window, and MIT-licensed weights. Z.ai designed it for what it calls "agentic engineering": long, multi-step coding and agent tasks rather than quick chat. GLM-5.1, 5.2 and 5.3 are later releases built on the same generation.

This explainer is based on Z.ai's official GLM-5 model card, developer documentation and pricing page, all reviewed November 19, 2026. Benchmark figures are Z.ai's own published results. We did not re-run them. GLM5 publishes this article and operates independently of Z.ai.

## GLM-5 at a Glance

GLM-5 

Made by | Z.ai (Zhipu AI) 
Released | February 2026 (official repository published February 11, 2026) 
Architecture | Mixture of experts: 744B total, 40B active parameters 
Pre-training data | 28.5T tokens 
Context window | 200K tokens 
Max output | 128K tokens 
Modalities | Text in, text out 
License | MIT 
API price (Z.ai) | $1.00 input / $0.20 cached input / $3.20 output per 1M tokens 

## What Changed From GLM-4.x to GLM-5

GLM-5 was a generational jump rather than a point release. Its official model card gives three concrete changes compared with GLM-4.5:

- About twice the scale. It grew from 355B total parameters (32B active) to 744B (40B active), and pre-training data went from 23T to 28.5T tokens.
- Sparse attention for cheaper long context. GLM-5 integrates DeepSeek Sparse Attention (DSA). Z.ai says this greatly reduces deployment cost while keeping long-context ability.
- A new reinforcement-learning system. Z.ai built slime, an asynchronous RL infrastructure, to make post-training faster and allow more fine-grained iterations.

Here is why the "40B active" figure matters more than the 744B headline. In a mixture-of-experts model, only a slice of the network runs for each token. You still need memory for all 744B parameters, but the compute per token is closer to a 40B dense model. So GLM-5 is expensive to host but relatively efficient to run once it's loaded.

## How Good Is GLM-5? Z.ai's Published Benchmarks

Against its predecessor GLM-4.7, Z.ai reports gains on nearly every benchmark it published:

Benchmark | GLM-4.7 | GLM-5 
---|---|---
SWE-bench Verified | 73.8 | 77.8 
SWE-bench Multilingual | 66.7 | 73.3 
Terminal-Bench 2.0 (Terminus 2) | 41.0 | 56.2 (60.7 on a verified version) 
BrowseComp | 52.0 | 62.0 
τ²-Bench | 87.4 | 89.7 
MCP-Atlas (public set) | 52.0 | 67.8 
Vending Bench 2 (simulated business) | $2,376.82 | $4,432.12 

The biggest jumps are in terminal tasks, tool use through MCP and long-running agent simulations. That matches Z.ai's positioning. Z.ai's documentation goes further and says GLM-5's real-world coding usability "approaches" Claude Opus 4.5. Treat that as the vendor's claim. On Z.ai's own table, Claude Opus 4.5 still scored higher on SWE-bench Verified (80.9).

A practical reading tip: look at Terminal-Bench and MCP-Atlas if you're building agents. Look at SWE-bench if you mostly want patches to existing code. GLM-5's improvement was largest on the agent-style benchmarks.

## GLM-5 vs GLM-5.1, 5.2 and 5.3

This is the most common point of confusion. In Z.ai's naming, GLM-5 is one model, and the point releases are separate models in the same generation:

Model | Released | Context | What it added 
---|---|---|---
GLM-5 | Feb 2026 | 200K | New 744B/40B-active base, DSA, slime RL 
GLM-5.1 | Apr 2026 | 200K | Much stronger long-horizon coding; SWE-Bench Pro gains 
GLM-5.2 | Jun 2026 | 1M | Solid 1M-token context, flexible thinking effort 
GLM-5.3 | Aug 2026 | 1M | Post-training upgrade on GLM-5.2's base; coding and cyber gains 

If an article says "GLM 5 has a 1M-token context," it's describing GLM-5.2 or 5.3, not the original GLM-5. If a provider lists "GLM 5" without a version number, check which model ID it actually serves.

For the later releases, see our explainers on GLM-5.1, GLM 5.2 and GLM 5.3.

## Is GLM-5 Open Source?

GLM-5's weights are published on Hugging Face under the MIT license, which allows commercial use, modification and redistribution as long as you keep the license notice. Z.ai also open-sourced the slime RL framework on GitHub.

What the open weights don't give you is cheap hardware. The model card lists vLLM (v0.19.0+), SGLang (v0.5.10+), KTransformers, Transformers and xLLM as supported serving stacks. A 744B-parameter checkpoint, though, needs a multi-GPU server even with quantization.

## Is GLM-5 Free?

The weights are free to download. Hosted access isn't free on Z.ai's standard API: the pricing page lists GLM-5 at $1.00 per million input tokens and $3.20 per million output tokens. That's cheaper than the GLM-5.1 and 5.2 rate of $1.40/$4.40, which makes GLM-5 the budget option within the 5.x generation if 200K context is enough for you.

For the full picture across every GLM model, see Is GLM free?

## Who Should Use GLM-5 Today?

GLM-5 is no longer Z.ai's flagship, but it has a clear niche:

- Use GLM-5 if you want 5.x-generation agent quality at the lowest 5.x price and your tasks fit within 200K tokens.
- Use GLM-5.2 or 5.3 if you need the 1M-token context or the strongest long-horizon coding.
- Stay on GLM-4.7 only if cost matters more than the GLM-5 gains shown above. GLM-4.7 is cheaper still at $0.60/$2.20.

Rule of thumb: start with the cheapest model that passes your five hardest real prompts, and move up only when it fails them. GLM5's API servesglm-5, glm-5.2 and glm-5.3 through one OpenAI-compatible endpoint, so comparing them is a one-word change in your code. Get the model IDs from the GLM5 API docs, or open GLM5 Chat and try a real task in your browser.

## Frequently Asked Questions

### What is GLM-5?

GLM-5 is Z.ai's February 2026 open-weight large language model. It's a 744B-parameter mixture-of-experts model with 40B active parameters, a 200K-token context and MIT-licensed weights, built for coding and agent tasks.

### Who made GLM-5?

Z.ai, the international brand of Zhipu AI. See what GLM is for the family background.

### Is GLM-5 open source?

Yes, in the open-weight sense. The weights are MIT-licensed on Hugging Face.

### Is GLM-5 free?

The weights are free. Z.ai's API charges $1.00 per million input tokens and $3.20 per million output tokens.

### What is GLM-5's context window?

200K tokens, with up to 128K output tokens, per Z.ai's documentation. The 1M-token context arrived with GLM-5.2.

### Is GLM-5 multimodal?

No. GLM-5 is text in, text out.

## The Bottom Line

GLM-5 is the model that opened Z.ai's fifth generation. It doubled the scale of GLM-4.5, added sparse attention and a new RL pipeline, and pushed open-weight agent benchmarks forward. Newer 5.x releases now outperform it, but its lower price keeps it useful for 200K-context agent work on a budget.

To see whether it's enough for your workload, try GLM-5 on a real task in GLM5 Chat, then compare it with GLM-5.2 on the same prompt.

import os
import json
import httpx
import openai
class FormulaChatClient:
def __init__(self, base_url: str, api_key: str):
"""初始化 Formula 客户端"""
self.base_url = base_url
self.api_key = api_key
self.openai = openai.Client(
base_url=base_url,
api_key=api_key,
)
self.httpx = httpx.Client(
base_url=base_url,
headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {api_key}"},
timeout=30.0,
)
# 使用 kimi-k3.1-pro，始终进行推理并启用 Preserved Thinking
self.model = "kimi-k3.1-pro"
def get_tools(self, formula_uri: str):
"""从 Formula API 获取工具定义"""
response = self.httpx.get(f"/formulas/{formula_uri}/tools")
response.raise_for_status() # 检查 HTTP 状态码
try:
return response.json().get("tools", [])
except json.JSONDecodeError as e:
print(f"错误: 无法解析响应为 JSON (状态码: {response.status_code})")
print(f"响应内容: {response.text[:500]}")
raise
def call_tool(self, formula_uri: str, function: str, args: dict):
"""调用官方工具"""
response = self.httpx.post(
f"/formulas/{formula_uri}/fibers",
json={"name": function, "arguments": json.dumps(args)},
)
response.raise_for_status() # 检查 HTTP 状态码
fiber = response.json()
if fiber.get("status", "") == "succeeded":
return fiber["context"].get("output") or fiber["context"].get("encrypted_output")
if "error" in fiber:
return f"Error: {fiber['error']}"
if "error" in fiber.get("context", {}):
return f"Error: {fiber['context']['error']}"
return "Error: Unknown error"
def close(self):
"""关闭客户端连接"""
self.httpx.close()
# 初始化客户端
base_url = os.getenv("MOONSHOT_BASE_URL", "https://api.moonshot.cn/v1")
api_key = os.getenv("MOONSHOT_API_KEY")
if not api_key:
raise ValueError("MOONSHOT_API_KEY 环境变量未设置，请先设置 API 密钥")
print(f"Base URL: {base_url}")
print(f"API Key: {api_key[:10]}...{api_key[-10:] if len(api_key) > 20 else api_key}\n")
client = FormulaChatClient(base_url, api_key)
# 定义要使用的官方工具 Formula URI
formula_uris = [
"moonshot/date:latest",
"moonshot/web-search:latest"
]
# 加载所有工具定义并建立映射
print("正在加载官方工具...")
all_tools = []
tool_to_uri = {} # function.name -> formula_uri 的映射
for uri in formula_uris:
try:
tools = client.get_tools(uri)
for tool in tools:
func = tool.get("function")
if func:
func_name = func.get("name")
if func_name:
tool_to_uri[func_name] = uri
all_tools.append(tool)
print(f" 已加载工具: {func_name} from {uri}")
except Exception as e:
print(f" 警告: 加载工具 {uri} 失败: {e}")
continue
print(f"总共加载 {len(all_tools)} 个工具\n")
if not all_tools:
raise ValueError("未能加载任何工具，请检查 API 密钥和网络连接")
# 初始化消息列表
messages = [
{
"role": "system",
"content": "你是 Kimi，一个专业的新闻分析师。你擅长收集、分析和整理信息，生成高质量的新闻报告。",
},
]
# 用户请求生成今日新闻报告
user_request = "请帮我生成一份今日新闻报告，包含重要的科技、经济和社会新闻。"
messages.append({
"role": "user",
"content": user_request
})
print(f"用户请求: {user_request}\n")
# 开始多步对话循环
max_iterations = 10 # 防止无限循环
for iteration in range(max_iterations):
# 调用模型
try:
completion = client.openai.chat.completions.create(
model=client.model,
messages=messages,
max_tokens=1024 * 32,
tools=all_tools,
)
except openai.AuthenticationError as e:
print(f"认证错误: {e}")
print("请检查 API key 是否正确，以及 API key 是否有权限访问该端点")
raise
except Exception as e:
print(f"调用模型时发生错误: {e}")
raise
# 获取响应
message = completion.choices[0].message
# 打印思考过程
if hasattr(message, "reasoning_content"):
print(f"=============第 {iteration + 1} 轮思考开始=============")
reasoning = getattr(message, "reasoning_content")
if reasoning:
print(reasoning[:500] + "..." if len(reasoning) > 500 else reasoning)
print(f"=============第 {iteration + 1} 轮思考结束=============\n")
# 添加 assistant 消息到上下文（保留 reasoning_content）
messages.append(message)
# 如果模型没有调用工具，说明对话结束
if not message.tool_calls:
print("=============最终回答=============")
print(message.content)
break
# 处理工具调用
print(f"模型决定调用 {len(message.tool_calls)} 个工具:\n")
for tool_call in message.tool_calls:
func_name = tool_call.function.name
args = json.loads(tool_call.function.arguments)
print(f"调用工具: {func_name}")
print(f"参数: {json.dumps(args, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2)}")
# 获取对应的 formula_uri
formula_uri = tool_to_uri.get(func_name)
if not formula_uri:
print(f"错误: 找不到工具 {func_name} 对应的 Formula URI")
continue
# 调用工具
result = client.call_tool(formula_uri, func_name, args)
# 打印结果（截断过长内容）
if len(str(result)) > 200:
print(f"工具结果: {str(result)[:200]}...\n")
else:
print(f"工具结果: {result}\n")
# 添加工具结果到消息列表
tool_message = {
"role": "tool",
"tool_call_id": tool_call.id,
"name": func_name,
"content": result
}
messages.append(tool_message)
print("\n对话完成！")
# 清理资源
client.close()

Kimi.title: Thinking Models - Kimi API Platform
Kimi.description: "Kimi K3.1 Pro is our flagship model for long-horizon ... with a 1M-token context window and industry-leading intelligence. The Kimi API Platform provides a range of large language model APIs with long context, multimodal understanding, and Tool Calling." ... {"socials":{"x":"https://x.com/Kimi_Moonshot","github":"https://github.com/MoonshotAI"...
Kimi.content:
Thinking models use reasoning tokens to “think” before producing a final answer — breaking down the problem, planning steps, and evaluating alternatives. The reasoning process is returned in the response’s reasoning_content field. Thinking before answering improves performance on complex reasoning, code generation, and multi-step tool calling, at the cost of higher latency and token usage.

Choose the right thinking model

This page uses the following thinking models:

kimi-k3.1-pro: the flagship thinking model; reasoning and Preserved Thinking are always on, and reasoning_content may be returned. Configure its reasoning effort with the top-level reasoning_effort request field, which supports "low" / "high" / "max" (default "max").

kimi-k3: supports a 1M-token context window and follows the same thinking behavior as K3.1 Pro.

kimi-k3.1-pro always reasons with Preserved Thinking always on; you do not need to (and should not) pass the thinking parameter — just set model, and optionally adjust reasoning effort with the top-level reasoning_effort field:

curl

python

$ curl https://api.moonshot.ai/v1/chat/completions \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $MOONSHOT_API_KEY" \ -d '{ "model": "kimi-k3.1-pro", "messages": [ { "role": "user", "content": "Prove that the square root of 2 is irrational." } ] }'

import osfrom openai import OpenAIclient = OpenAI( api_key=os.environ["MOONSHOT_API_KEY"], base_url="https://api.moonshot.ai/v1",)completion = client.chat.completions.create( model="kimi-k3.1-pro", messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Prove that the square root of 2 is irrational."}],)message = completion.choices[0].messageif hasattr(message, "reasoning_content"): print(getattr(message, "reasoning_content"))print(message.content)

For multi-turn conversations and tool calls, pass the complete assistant message returned by the API back to messages as-is (including reasoning_content); see Preserved Thinking. For more K3.1 Pro usage, see the Kimi K3.1 Pro Quickstart.

Control thinking behavior

K3.1 Pro: adjust reasoning effort with reasoning_effort

kimi-k3.1-pro always reasons and does not support the thinking parameter. Adjust reasoning effort with the top-level reasoning_effort field ("low" / "high" / "max", default "max"); see Reasoning Effort for usage and examples.

Read reasoning_content from the response

When using a thinking model with thinking enabled, the API response carries the model’s reasoning in the reasoning_content field. When reading this field:

In the OpenAI SDK, ChoiceDelta and ChatCompletionMessage types do not provide a reasoning_content field directly, so you cannot access it via .reasoning_content. You must use hasattr(obj, "reasoning_content") to check if the field exists, and if so, use getattr(obj, "reasoning_content") to retrieve its value.

If you use other frameworks or directly interface with the HTTP API, you can directly obtain the reasoning_content field at the same level as the content field.

In streaming output (stream=True), the reasoning_content field will always appear before the content field. In your business logic, you can detect if the content field has been output to determine if the reasoning (inference process) is finished.

Tokens in reasoning_content are also controlled by the max_tokens parameter: the sum of tokens in reasoning_content and content must be less than or equal to max_tokens.

Configure multi-step tool calls

Thinking models can perform deep reasoning across multiple tool calls to tackle complex tasks. To get reliable results, always follow these configuration rules when using thinking models:

In both single-task tool-call loops and multi-turn conversations, pass the complete assistant message back as-is, including reasoning_content. kimi-k3.1-pro and kimi-k3 always enable Preserved Thinking.

Set max_tokens >= 16000 to ensure the full reasoning_content and content can be returned without truncation.

Do not set temperature.kimi-k3.1-pro and kimi-k3 fix temperature at 1.0; do not pass it explicitly (see Model Parameter Reference).

Enable streaming (stream=True). Because thinking models return both reasoning_content and regular content, the response is larger than usual. Streaming delivers a better user experience and helps avoid network-timeout issues.

Complete example: generate a daily news report

The example below demonstrates a “Daily News Report Generation” scenario. The model will sequentially call official tools like date (to get the date) and web_search (to search today’s news), and will present deep reasoning throughout this process:

import osimport jsonimport httpximport openaiclass FormulaChatClient: def __init__(self, base_url: str, api_key: str): """Initialize Formula client""" self.base_url = base_url self.api_key = api_key self.openai = openai.Client( base_url=base_url, api_key=api_key, ) self.httpx = httpx.Client( base_url=base_url, headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {api_key}"}, timeout=30.0, ) # Use kimi-k3.1-pro; reasoning and Preserved Thinking are always enabled self.model = "kimi-k3.1-pro" def get_tools(self, formula_uri: str): """Get tool definitions from Formula API""" response = self.httpx.get(f"/formulas/{formula_uri}/tools") response.raise_for_status() try: return response.json().get("tools", []) except json.JSONDecodeError as e: print(f"Error: Unable to parse JSON (status code: {response.status_code})") print(f"Response content: {response.text[:500]}") raise def call_tool(self, formula_uri: str, function: str, args: dict): """Call an official tool""" response = self.httpx.post( f"/formulas/{formula_uri}/fibers", json={"name": function, "arguments": json.dumps(args)}, ) response.raise_for_status() fiber = response.json() if fiber.get("status", "") == "succeeded": return fiber["context"].get("output") or fiber["context"].get("encrypted_output") if "error" in fiber: return f"Error: {fiber['error']}" if "error" in fiber.get("context", {}): return f"Error: {fiber['context']['error']}" return "Error: Unknown error" def close(self): """Close the client connection""" self.httpx.close()# Initialize clientbase_url = os.getenv("MOONSHOT_BASE_URL", "https://api.moonshot.ai/v1")api_key = os.getenv("MOONSHOT_API_KEY")if not api_key: raise ValueError("MOONSHOT_API_KEY environment variable not set. Please set your API key.")print(f"Base URL: {base_url}")print(f"API Key: {api_key[:10]}...{api_key[-10:] if len(api_key) > 20 else api_key}\n")client = FormulaChatClient(base_url, api_key)# Define the official tool Formula URIs to useformula_uris = [ "moonshot/date:latest", "moonshot/web-search:latest"]# Load all tool definitions and build mappingprint("Loading official tools...")all_tools = []tool_to_uri = {} # function.name -> formula_urifor uri in formula_uris: try: tools = client.get_tools(uri) for tool in tools: func = tool.get("function") if func: func_name = func.get("name") if func_name: tool_to_uri[func_name] = uri all_tools.append(tool) print(f" Loaded tool: {func_name} from {uri}") except Exception as e: print(f" Warning: Failed to load tool {uri}: {e}") continueprint(f"Loaded {len(all_tools)} tools in total\n")if not all_tools: raise ValueError("No tools loaded. Please check API key and network connection.")# Initialize message listmessages = [ { "role": "system", "content": "You are Kimi, a professional news analyst. You excel at collecting, analyzing, and organizing information to generate high-quality news reports.", },]# User request to generate today's news reportuser_request = "Please help me generate a daily news report including important technology, economy, and society news."messages.append({ "role": "user", "content": user_request})print(f"User request: {user_request}\n")# Begin multi-step conversation loopmax_iterations = 10 # Prevent infinite loopsfor iteration in range(max_iterations): try: completion = client.openai.chat.completions.create( model=client.model, messages=messages, max_tokens=1024 * 32, tools=all_tools, ) except openai.AuthenticationError as e: print(f"Authentication error: {e}") print("Please check if the API key is correct and has the required permissions") raise except Exception as e: print(f"Error while calling the model: {e}") raise # Get response message = completion.choices[0].message # Print reasoning process if hasattr(message, "reasoning_content"): print(f"=============Reasoning round {iteration + 1} starts=============") reasoning = getattr(message, "reasoning_content") if reasoning: print(reasoning[:500] + "..." if len(reasoning) > 500 else reasoning) print(f"=============Reasoning round {iteration + 1} ends=============\n") # Add assistant message to context (preserve reasoning_content) messages.append(message) # If the model did not call any tools, conversation is done if not message.tool_calls: print("=============Final Answer=============") print(message.content) break # # 功能总览

Source: https://platform.kimi.com/docs/features

按模型推理、工具调用、生态集成和托管智能体查看 Kimi 开放平台的主要能力，并跳转到对应使用文档。

通过本页了解 Kimi 开放平台已经提供的能力，并跳转到对应文档。首次使用时，建议先阅读快速开始；需要查询接口定义时，请查看 API 概述。

每项能力的适用模型、接口、区域和计费方式以对应文档为准。

## 模型推理功能

### 模型能力

功能 | 说明 
---|---
思考模式 | 使用推理能力处理复杂任务、多步工具调用和 Agent 工作流，并在多轮对话中正确保留思考内容。 
↳ 推理强度 | 按模型支持的档位调节推理深度、延迟和 Token 消耗。 
多轮对话 | 在无状态 API 中维护消息历史，并控制上下文长度。 
流式输出 | 通过 SSE 增量接收响应，降低首 Token 等待时间并边生成边处理内容。 
多模态输入 | 向支持多模态的 Kimi 模型传入文本、图片和视频。 
Structured Output | 使用 JSON Schema 约束输出字段和类型，让下游系统更稳定地解析结果。 
JSON Mode | 要求模型输出合法的 JSON Object，但不约束具体字段结构。 
Partial Mode | 续写给定的 assistant 文本、固定回复开头，或继续被截断的输出。 
上下文缓存 | 复用重复的请求前缀，并通过 5m 或 1h 缓存时长降低输入成本。 

### API 接口

功能 | 说明 
---|---
Chat Completions API | 使用 OpenAI 兼容格式发起对话、生成结构化输出或调用工具。 
Responses API | 使用 OpenAI Responses 兼容格式生成文本或 JSON，并调用函数工具或服务端联网搜索。 
Messages API | 使用 Anthropic Messages 兼容格式接入 Kimi，支持 Anthropic SDK 和 Claude Code 等工具。 

### 工具调用

功能 | 说明 
---|---
自定义工具调用 | 定义函数工具，在应用中执行模型发起的调用，并将结果回传给模型。 
↳ 工具调用约束 | 使用 tool_choice 让模型自动选择、强制或禁止工具调用。 
↳ 动态加载工具 | 按需追加工具定义，减少 Token 消耗并保留前缀缓存。 
↳ Kimi K3 工具调用最佳实践 | 结合动态加载、tool_choice 和推理强度设计工具调用流程。 
官方工具 | 通过 Chat Completions API 配置和调用 Kimi 开放平台提供的官方工具。 
联网搜索 | 按场景选择搜索接口、控制成本并优化查询词和参数。 
↳ 联网搜索 Basic | 通过独立接口获取网页标题、摘要、站点和链接等结构化搜索结果。 
↳ 联网搜索 Pro | 获取按相关性排序的正文片段，并按站点和时间范围约束结果。 
网页抓取 | 抓取指定 URL 的网页标题和 Markdown 正文。 

### 核心工作流

功能 | 说明 
---|---
文件问答 | 上传并抽取文件内容，将其加入对话以完成单文件或多文件问答。 
↳ Files API | 上传文件并获取文件 ID，也可列出、查询、下载或删除文件。 
Batch API | 上传 JSONL 请求并异步创建、查询和下载大规模批处理结果。 
控制台批量推理 | 无需编写代码，在控制台创建、监控并下载批量推理结果。 
自动断线重连 | 为流式请求实现断线重连，并结合 Partial Mode 从中断处继续生成。 
Token 计算 | 在发送请求前估算消息内容的 Token 数量。 

### 生态集成

功能 | 说明 
---|---
Kimi Code CLI | 使用开放平台 API Key 接入、切换和更新 Kimi Code CLI。 
Codex | 通过 Responses API 将 Codex 接入 Kimi，并完成配置和连接验证。 
Claude Code | 将 Kimi API 接入 Claude Code，完成模型选择和配置验证。 
OpenClaw | 在 OpenClaw 中连接 Kimi API 并构建跨平台智能体。 
OpenCode | 在 OpenCode 中接入 Kimi 模型并配置推理强度。 
Hermes Agent | 在 Hermes Agent 中接入 Kimi，使用文本和多模态理解能力。 
ModelScope MCP | 在 Playground 中同步并启用 ModelScope 托管的 MCP 服务。 

### 调试与运维

功能 | 说明 
---|---
Playground | 比较模型、调整参数、测试工具调用，并将调试结果转换为 API 请求。 
MoonPalace | 调试 Kimi API，管理对话、参数、文件、工具调用和上下文缓存。 
组织、项目与 API Key 管理 | 管理组织和项目层级、预算与限速、成员、IP 白名单及消费分析。 
Admin API | 将成员、项目和密钥管理，以及账单、用量和审计查询接入企业现有系统。 
零数据保留 ZDR | 了解面向企业客户提供的零数据保留模式。 

## 托管智能体功能

Kimi Hosted Agents 将 Agent 运行所需的 Harness 作为云端服务提供。产品形态和适用场景见产品概览，首次使用可从快速开始进入。你也可以通过控制台或 kha CLI 使用托管智能体；从自建智能体循环迁移时，请参考迁移指南。

功能 | 说明 
---|---
智能体 | 创建、更新、版本管理和归档托管智能体的配置对象。 
权限策略 | 配置工具直接放行或执行前等待客户端确认，并查看权限评估结果。 
技能 | 为智能体挂载版本化技能包，按需扩展能力。 
MCP | 声明 MCP 服务并通过凭据库注入访问凭据，让智能体调用第三方 MCP 工具。 
插件 | 创建、管理和引用官方或自定义插件，并在智能体中完成配置。 
工具 | 使用内置与自定义工具，并按需加载工具定义。 
执行环境 | 配置云环境的预装依赖、网络访问策略和初始化脚本；需要自有基础设施时，使用自托管环境。 
会话 | 创建会话、绑定执行环境和资源、发送任务，并管理会话生命周期或取消当前轮次。 
事件流 | 通过 SSE 订阅会话和线程事件，读取历史事件并在断线后继续接收。 
凭据库 | 保存第三方服务凭据，在创建会话时绑定，并管理授权、轮换和归档。 
文件 | 上传文件、在会话中绑定文件，并浏览或下载会话文件。 
记忆 | 创建可跨会话使用的记忆库，按版本管理文件，并通过梦境自动整理记忆。 
多智能体编排 | 配置智能体之间的任务委派，在同一会话中运行子线程并观察执行状态。 
定时任务 | 使用 cron 定时或手动运行智能体，查看运行记录并管理触发器。 

## 相关索引

索引 | 说明 
---|---
模型列表 | 查看当前可用模型和已下线模型的迁移提示。 
API 概述 | 查看服务地址、认证方式、协议兼容性和完整端点清单。 
模型参数参考 | 对比各模型系列的默认参数、可调范围和使用约束。 
模型推理定价 | 查看模型 Token 与上下文缓存的计费说明。 
托管智能体定价 | 查看模型 Token、沙箱运行时长和插件调用的计费说明。 
充值与限速 | 查看充值方式、速率限制和相关规则。 
问题排查 | 排查账号、计费、认证、模型参数、限速和网络连接等常见问题。

Kimi.content:
Learn the core Kimi API concepts behind models, prompts, tokens, context windows, streaming, tool calling, and multimodal input.

Text and Multimodal Models

kimi-k3.1-pro is Kimi’s flagship model, built for long-horizon coding and end-to-end knowledge work, with native visual understanding; when you need faster output, choose the high-speed variant kimi-k3.1-pro-highspeed. The input to a model is commonly called a “prompt”, and clear instructions plus representative examples are the most effective way to get stable outputs. Other models are also available — see the Model List for details.

Language Model Inference Service

The language model inference service is an API service based on the pretrained models developed and trained by us (Moonshot AI). Today, the platform offers three interfaces — Chat Completions, Responses, and Messages (Anthropic-compatible) — for conversation, code generation, visual understanding, and agent tasks. Models do not directly access external resources such as the internet or databases by default, but you can extend them with official tools or custom tool calls when needed.

Token

Text generation models process text in units called Tokens. A Token represents a common sequence of characters. For example, a single English character like “antidisestablishmentarianism” might be broken down into a combination of several Tokens, while a short and common phrase like “word” might be represented by a single Token. Generally speaking, for a typical English text, 1 Token is roughly equivalent to 3-4 English characters.It is important to note that the total length of Input and Output cannot exceed the selected model’s maximum context length. For example, kimi-k3.1-pro supports a context window of up to 1M tokens. For other models’ context lengths, see the Model List.

Rate Limits

How do these rate limits work?Rate limits are measured in four ways: concurrency, RPM (requests per minute), TPM (tokens per minute), and TPD (tokens per day). The rate limit can be reached in any of these categories, depending on which one is hit first. For example, you might send 20 requests to ChatCompletions, each with only 100 Tokens, and you would hit the limit (if your RPM limit is 20), even if you haven’t reached 200k Tokens in those 20 requests (assuming your TPM limit is 200k).For the gateway, for convenience, we calculate rate limits based on the max_completion_tokens parameter in the request. This means that if your request includes the max_completion_tokens parameter, we will use this parameter to calculate the rate limit. If your request does not include the max_completion_tokens parameter, we will use the default max_completion_tokens parameter to calculate the rate limit. After you make a request, we will determine whether you have reached the rate limit based on the number of Tokens in your request plus the number of max_completion_tokens in your parameter, regardless of the actual number of Tokens generated.In the billing process, we calculate the cost based on the number of Tokens in your request plus the actual number of Tokens generated.

Other Important Notes:

Rate limits are enforced at the user level, not the key level.

Currently, we share rate limits across all models.

Model List

For all available models and their capabilities, see the Model List page.

Usage Guide

Getting an API Key

You need an API key to use our service. You can create an API key in our Console.

Sending Requests

You can use our Chat Completions API to send requests. You need to provide an API key and a model name. You can choose to use the default max_completion_tokens parameter or customize the max_completion_tokens parameter. You can refer to the Chat API documentation for the calling method.

Handling Responses

Generally, we set a 2 hours timeout. If a single request exceeds this time, we will return a 504 error. If your request exceeds the rate limit, we will return a 429 error. If your request is successful, we will return a response in JSON format.If you need to quickly process some tasks, you can use the non-streaming mode of our Chat Completions API. In this mode, we will return all the generated text in one request. If you need more control, you can use the streaming mode. In this mode, we will return an SSE stream, where you can obtain the generated text. This can provide a better user experience, and you can also interrupt the request at any time without wasting resources.

Build with the Grok API: intelligent, fast, and cost-effective models across code, text, voice, image, and video.
import { xai } from "@ai-sdk/xai";
import { generateText } from "ai";

const { text } = await generateText({
  model: xai.responses("grok-4.7"),
  prompt: "Fix this function and explain the bug: function median(a){a.sort();return a[a.length/2]}",
});

console.log(text);from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(
    api_key="<YOUR_XAI_API_KEY_HERE>",
    base_url="https://api.x.ai/v1",
)

response = client.responses.create(
    model="grok-4.7",

xAI.description: The Grok chatbot tool was designed by Elon Musk's SpaceX Super Intelligence to generate sexualised and offensive images, an MP suing the company has said. ... SpaceXSI – formerly known as xAI – filed a defence to the ... in which it admits the ... to create deepfakes.
xAI.content:
# MP says Grok was designed to make sexualised images

The Grok chatbot tool was designed by Elon Musk's SpaceX Super Intelligence to generate sexualised and offensive images, an MP suing the company has said.

Jess Asato, Labour MP for Lowestoft in Suffolk, is suing SpaceXSI for damages after sexualised images and videos, including some depicting her being sexually assaulted, were generated and shared online using the AI tool.

Her claim alleges SpaceXSI's design choices make them responsible for Grok's output, and that the company misused her private information and breached data protection rules.

SpaceXSI previously said users would no longer be able to use the tool to generate sexualised images of real people.

In court documents published earlier this year, lawyers for Ms Asato claimed she was "victimised" after speaking out against the creation of non-consensual deepfake images of women by Grok.

Marie Demetriou KC, for Ms Asato, said the MP had posted on X on 6 January calling on Musk to "understand that using AI to strip women without their consent is sexual assault designed to degrade and humiliate".

In the days that followed, several X users prompted Grok to create "sexualised, intimate, grossly offensive, degrading, threatening, humiliating and/or discriminatory non-consensual images" of Ms Asato, which were disseminated online, the lawsuit stated.

SpaceXSI also had a "spicy mode" service for Grok which resulted in the AI chatbot generating "more sexual" content, with Grok's system prompts containing the instructions "no restrictions on adult sexual content or offensive content", according to the MP.

After multiple attempts to report some posts, X refused to remove them, stating in March that they did not violate its terms of service, privacy policy or rules.

Demetriou said that while two videos were later removed, six of 21 posts reported in February remained live as of late July.

The company changed its policy regarding Grok's "spicy mode" in January so that it was only available to paying Grok subscribers, she added.

According to the MP, SpaceXSI – formerly known as xAI – filed a defence to the legal action on 30 October in which it admits the chatbot is designed to expand on short user prompts by pulling data from X threads and the wider internet to create deepfakes.

"Grok is not a passive tool at the mercy of its users," Asato said.

"It is engineered and designed to turn a two-word prompt into fake but realistic, degrading imagery."

She is also asking the High Court to order that SpaceXSI "comply with existing laws to make its system safe for all".

It is illegal to create or request a non-consensual deepfake image of an adult in the UK.

"If an AI product cannot be deployed without automating the humiliation of women at scale, it should not be deployed at all," Asato continued.

"I am taking this case forward to establish a clear principle: tech companies must be held accountable for the harm their systems actively generate."

#### Release Notes

# Release Notes

## November

November 19

### grok-build-0.1 end of life

grok-build-0.1 reached end of life on November 19, 2026 and is no longer served on the API.

November 2

### grok-imagine-image-quality retired

Requests togrok-imagine-image-quality and grok-imagine-image-pro are now served by grok-imagine-image-2.0-low: grok-imagine-image-2.0 with quality set to low, at a lower per-image price. No request changes are needed. usage.cost_in_usd_ticks on each response reflects the lower price, and gRPC responses (xAI SDK) report grok-imagine-image-2.0-low as the model. See the migration guide.

## October

October 27

### Custom moderation controls

You can now set content guidelines on text API requests. Add aguidelines array to a Chat Completions or Responses API request to set how Grok handles content in the nsfw, violence, and profanity categories. Grok follows the guidelines as it writes its response. See Custom Moderation Controls.

October 14

### Grok Voice 3.0 is available

grok-voice-3.0 is now available with Speech to Speech, at the same price as Grok Voice 2.0. grok-voice-latest now points to grok-voice-3.0, so sessions that use the alias are upgraded automatically. The API is unchanged. To get started, see the Speech to Speech docs.

October 14

### Grok Voice 2.0 deprecation

grok-voice-2.0 is deprecated. To upgrade, set model to grok-voice-3.0 or grok-voice-latest, at the same price. See Upgrading from Grok Voice 2.0.

October 2

### grok-voice-transcribe-1.0 end of life

grok-voice-transcribe-1.0 is deprecated and reaches end of life on October 2, 2026. All requests to that slug are routed to grok-voice-transcribe-2.0 at the same price, with higher accuracy. See the Speech to Text docs.

## September

September 25

### safety_identifier request field

You can now sendsafety_identifier, an opaque end-user identifier assigned by your application, on Chat Completions, the Responses API, deferred chat completions, the Batch API, and the gRPC GetCompletionsRequest. It lets SpaceXSI attribute a policy violation to one of your end users rather than to your API key. The legacy user field is still accepted. See the Security FAQ.

September 21

### Grok 4.7

Grok 4.7, SpaceXSI's frontier model for coding, agentic tasks, and knowledge work, is now available on the xAI API asgrok-4.7. It has a 500k context window, text and image inputs with text-only output, and no text output limit. Pricing is $2 / $0.50 / $6 per 1M tokens (input / cached input / output) below 200k prompt tokens, and $4 / $1 / $12 above. Reasoning effort supports low, medium, high (default), and xhigh. On the Responses API, grok-4.7 always returns reasoning.encrypted_content, even when include does not list it. It is also served on the US regional endpoint. Grok 4.7 Fast is the same model and costs 2x the standard token rates, or 1.5x for long-context requests. It's available only in Cursor and Grok Build, not on the public xAI API, and is billed through your plan there. See the Grok 4.7 overview and the announcement.

September 17

### Grok Voice Transcribe 2.0

grok-voice-transcribe-2.0 is now available. Use grok-voice-transcribe-1.0 or grok-voice-transcribe-2.0; the default is grok-voice-transcribe-2.0. See the Speech to Text docs.

September 2

### grok-imagine-image-quality retirement on November 2

On November 2, 2026,grok-imagine-image-quality is retired. Requests to the slug will be served by grok-imagine-image-2.0 with quality set to low, with no change to the request or response shape and at a lower per-image price. grok-imagine-image (1.0) is not affected. See the migration guide.

## August

August 28

### Image API updates

- Auto quality. Thequality parameter on grok-imagine-image-2.0 now accepts auto, and the default when quality is omitted has moved from medium to auto. Auto currently uses low for image generation and medium for image editing. Images are billed at the quality they are served at. Pass low or medium explicitly to pin a specific quality. See Image Generation.
- Five reference images. Image editing now accepts up to 5 source images per request (was 3). See Multi-Image Editing.
- New aspect ratios. Image generation and editing accept21:9 (cinematic widescreen) and 5:2 (wide banners). See Image Generation.

August 12

### Grok 4.6

Grok 4.6, SpaceXSI's frontier model for coding, agentic tasks, and knowledge work, is now available on the xAI API. It has a 500k context window, text and image inputs with text-only output, and no text output limit. Pricing is $2 / $0.50 / $6 per 1M tokens (input / cached input / output) below 200k prompt tokens, and $4 / $1 / $12 above. Reasoning effort supports low, medium, high (default), and xhigh. See the Grok 4.6 overview and the announcement.

August 11

### Grok Bot

Grok Bot is now available. Durable AI teammates that work on a persistent cloud computer, with messaging, approvals, connectors, and routines. See the Grok Bot overview and Get started.

## July

July 31

### grok-imagine-video-1.5 modalities

grok-imagine-video-1.5 now supports text-to-video, image-to-video, and reference-to-video (including optional preset voices), with native 1080p for T2V and I2V. Text-to-video on this model runs as text-to-image then image-to-video under the hood. See Video Generation, Image-to-Video, and Reference-to-Video.

July 29

### Grok Voice 2.0 is available

grok-voice-2.0 is now available with Speech to Speech. grok-voice-latest will route to this model starting August 5, 2026. To get started, see the Speech to Speech docs. For more details, see our announcement.

July 23

### Adjustable VAD threshold for Speech to Text

Speech to Text now accepts avad_threshold parameter (streaming query param and batch multipart field) to tune the voice-activity gate that skips non-speech audio. Lower values transcribe quieter or noisier speech — useful for narrowband telephony — and 0 disables the gate. See the Speech to Text docs.

July 17

### Grok 4.5 available in the EU

Grok 4.5 is now available in the API console for EU users. See the Grok 4.5 overview.

July 8

### Grok 4.5

Grok 4.5, SpaceXSI's model for coding, agentic tasks, and knowledge work, is now available on the xAI API. Priced at $2 / 1M input tokens and $6 / 1M output tokens, with configurable reasoning effort (low, medium, or high; default high). See the Grok 4.5 overview and the announcement.

## June

June 15

### Priority Processing

You can now request higher scheduling priority per request by settingservice_tier: "priority" on text inference endpoints (Chat Completions and Responses). The response's service_tier field reports the tier actually applied, and priority rates are billed only when priority is used. For more details, see the Priority Processing docs.

June 10

### Public URLs and Files API ↔ image & video integration

- Public URLs for Files — turn any file in your Files API storage into a permanent, unauthenticated URL that anyone can open, embed, or share. Revocable at any time, or set an auto-expiry between 1 hour and 30 days. See the Public URLs docs.

## May

May 29

### Smart Turn for Streaming STT

The streaming Speech to Text API now supports Smart Turn end-of-turn detection. When enabled via thesmart_turn query parameter, an ML model predicts whether the speaker has finished their thought at silence boundaries — reducing false endpointing during dictation, number sequences, and mid-sentence pauses. Use smart_turn_timeout to set a maximum silence fallback. For more details, see the Smart Turn docs.

May 29

### Context Compaction

The Context Compaction API is now available. You can shrink long conversations into a shorter context and reuse it in follow-up requests for lower cost, faster time-to-first-token, and sharper responses on long agent loops. For more details, see the Context Compaction docs.

### WebSocket Responses API Mode

WebSocket Responses API mode is now available. Drive the Responses API over a single, long-lived WebSocket connection for lower end-to-end latency on tool-heavy agent workloads. For more details, see the WebSocket Mode docs.

May 27

### Image Search in Web Search

Web Search now supports explicitly searching for images. Enableenable_image_search to let Grok search directly for relevant images; responses can include returned images as Markdown image embeds. For details, see Enable Image Search.

May 19

### Grok Build 0.1

SpaceXSI's coding model, trained specifically for agentic coding workflows. Currently in early access.

The model slug isgrok-build-0.1.

May 14

### Grok Build

Grok Build is now available in beta. Use the interactive TUI, run headlessly in scripts, or build apps and orchestrators with the Agent Client Protocol.

Install with a single command:

Bash
curl -fsSL https://x.ai/cli/install.sh | bash

For more details, see the Grok Build docs.

May 1

### Custom Voices

You can now clone a voice from a short audio clip and use it across the Text-to-Speech and Speech to Speech APIs. Create and manage your voice catalog from the SpaceXSI console. For more details, check out the Custom Voices docs and our blog post.

Apr 30

Every API response now includes the exact cost of the request via acost_in_usd_ticks field in the usage object. Works across chat completions, Responses API, image generation, video generation, and streaming. For more details, see the

client = OpenAI(base_url="https://api.ofox.ai/v1", api_key=os.environ["OFOX_API_KEY"])

resp = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="x-ai/grok-4.7",
    reasoning_effort="low",
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Explain idempotency in one sentence."}],
)
print(resp.choices[0].message.content)
print("Reasoning tokens:", resp.usage.completion_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens)

## Reasoning

Key pointGrok 4.7, 4.6, and 4.5 always reason, and complex questions may take several minutes. Use reasoning_effort: low to reduce the amount of reasoning, or switch to the non-reasoning Grok 4.1 Fast.

Model | Reasoning | reasoning_effort 
---|---|---
Grok 4.7, 4.6, 4.5 | Always reason | low significantly reduces reasoning 
Grok 4.3 | Always reasons; reasoning content is not returned | Accepted 
Grok 4.1 Fast, 4.20 | No reasoning | Returns 400 on Grok 4.1 Fast 

Measured on the same math problem: by default Grok 4.7 used about 15,000 reasoning tokens and took about 4 minutes; withreasoning_effort: "low", it used about 4,200 tokens and took about 1 minute. Reasoning tokens are billed at the output rate, and their count is in usage.completion_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens; reasoning content is in delta.reasoning_content of the streaming response.

## Other features

- Image input: supported by Grok 4.3, 4.20, and 4.1 Fast, using standardimage_url content blocks; see Vision for the format.
- Structured output and tool calling:response_format supports json_schema; tool calling uses the standard tools parameter.
- Caching: repeated request prefixes are cached automatically; the hit count is inusage.prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens.

## Common errors

HTTP · type | Error message | Cause | Fix 
---|---|---|---
400 invalid_request_error | Contains This model does not support and reasoning | reasoning_effort was sent to the non-reasoning model Grok 4.1 Fast | Remove the parameter 
400 protocol_not_supported | Model 'x-ai/grok-4.7' does not support the 'anthropic' protocol on this platform. | The model does not support the Anthropic API | Use the OpenAI-compatible API 
400 endpoint_not_supported | Model 'x-ai/grok-4.7' does not support the /v1/responses endpoint on this platform. | The model does not support the Responses API | Use /v1/chat/completions 
404 model_not_found | Model 'xai/grok-4.7' not found | The prefix was written as xai/ | The prefix is x-ai/ 
Request timeout | — | Reasoning takes too long | Pass reasoning_effort: "low", use streaming, or set the client timeout to 600 seconds or more 

For other general errors, see Error handling.

## Official docs

## FAQ

How do I write Grok model IDs?

The standard form is x-ai/grok-4.7; you can also omit the prefix and write grok-4.7. Writing xai/grok-4.7 returns 404.

Why is Grok 4.7 so slow?

Grok 4.7, 4.6, and 4.5 always reason, and complex questions may use more than ten thousand reasoning tokens and take several minutes. Passing reasoning_effort: "low" shortens this significantly, or switch to the non-reasoning Grok 4.1 Fast.

Can reasoning be turned off for Grok?

Reasoning cannot be turned off for Grok 4.7, 4.6, 4.5, or 4.3; you can only reduce it with reasoning_effort. For fast responses, use Grok 4.1 Fast.

Can Claude Code use Grok?

Only Grok 4.3 supports the Anthropic API; calls to other Grok models return protocol_not_supported.

How long a context does Grok support?

Grok 4.1 Fast and 4.20 support 2M tokens, Grok 4.3 supports 1M, and Grok 4.7, 4.6, and 4.5 support 500K.

# Model Release Notes

Review OpenAI model releases, capability updates, retirements, and changes to the Model Spec.

Updated: 前天

# November 17, 2026

## GPT-6.2 Astra and GPT-6.2 Sol in the OpenAI API

We’re introducing GPT-6.2 Astra and GPT-6.2 Sol in the OpenAI API. Astra is our frontier model for applications that need advanced reasoning, coding, and the ability to handle complex professional work. Sol combines speed and lower cost with the ability to work through tasks that take several steps. Both improve on their predecessors’ results on demanding tasks while generating fewer output tokens.
Use gpt-6.2-astra or gpt-6.2-sol with the Responses or Chat Completions API. Both models accept text and images and return text, and review Standard API rates.

# November 16, 2026

## OpenAI CSAM image classifier

The OpenAI CSAM (Child Sexual Abuse Material) Image Classifier helps approved organizations review images for potential CSAM, including AI-generated material. Access is available through the OpenAI API at no cost and requires approval.

The classifier returns scores that can help trained reviewers prioritize review. It does not replace human judgment. Organizations remain responsible for reviewing results and deciding what action to take, including any reporting obligations.

Access requires an application, verification, program onboarding, and acceptance of the applicable terms. For application instructions, see: Requesting access to the OpenAI CSAM Image Classifier.

# October 30, 2026

## GPT-6 Rosalind Research

GPT-6 Rosalind Research brings GPT-6 reasoning capabilities to multistep life sciences research, with safeguards designed for biological work. It is rolling out to a limited set of approved Research customers in Work, Codex, and the API. It is not available in the Chat tab.

Access requires Rosalind Research approval for your organization and authorized users. Discovery approval does not grant Research access. Customers can continue to use GPT-5.5 Rosalind Research, and Rosalind Discovery remains on 5.5. On the API, usegpt-6-rosalind.

In Enterprise workspaces, the model starts in a two-week Admin Preview and is off by default. Admins can enable approved Research users and configure access for after the preview.

For access and setup, see: GPT-Rosalind for life sciences research. For pricing, see: API pricing, the credit-based rate card, or the Enterprise token-based rate card.

# October 29, 2026

## GPT-6 in ChatGPT update

We’re updating GPT-6 in Chat to give more concise responses and reduce overly flattering language. This update applies to Free and Go users, and people using ChatGPT without signing in.

On Plus and Pro, it applies only to the model ChatGPT can switch to after you reach GPT-6 message limits. The main GPT-6 model on Plus and Pro is unchanged.

## Updates to the OpenAI Model Spec

We’ve updated the Model Spec, our public description of how we want our models to behave. The revision reorganizes its guidance around five values: faithfulness to human intent, harm minimization, honesty and transparency, human agency, and care. It clarifies how GPT should understand human intent and exercise judgment in unfamiliar situations while remaining faithful to human direction and oversight.

Alongside clearer explanations of existing principles, the update adds guidance on context, memory, personalization, human agency, and oversight, and revises guidance on controlling and communicating side effects. It also adjusts some behavioral defaults and retires most detailed style guidance. Throughout the Spec, we now refer to the model as “GPT” rather than “the assistant,” reflecting its broader range of uses.

Read more about the changes and their rationale in our blog post, or explore the updated Model Spec.

# October 26, 2026

## GPT-6.1 Terra

GPT-6.1 Terra is rolling out in the OpenAI API as gpt-6.1-terra and in ChatGPT Work and Codex. It supports a range of tasks, including visual reasoning, computer use, and writing.

Standard API pricing is $1 per million input tokens, $0.05 per million cached input tokens, and $5 per million output tokens. API usage is billed separately from ChatGPT subscriptions.

In ChatGPT, Terra is available in Work and Codex, not Chat. It does not support UAE inference residency; this restriction is based on where inference runs, not your location.

For API capabilities and availability, see: Model directory. For help choosing a model in Work or Codex, see: Models.

# October 14, 2026

## Retiring GPT-5.5

We’re retiring GPT-5.5 from ChatGPT, ChatGPT Work, and Codex. This change does not affect API access.

# August 18, 2026

## Updates to the OpenAI Model Spec

We’ve updated the Model Spec, our living document outlining intended model behavior.

This update adds additional clarity around principles on appropriate relational interactions for teens. It also clarifies how assistants should handle false or unsupported premises, removes outdated guidance for pre-reasoning models, adds a new section "Be clear about capabilities and limits", and makes a few other small changes and copy edits.

More information on our principles related to teens can be found in our ChatGPT for Teens blog post, and the latest version of the Model Spec is available at model-spec.openai.com.

# July 9, 2026

## Introducing GPT-5.6 Sol in ChatGPT

We’re beginning the rollout of GPT-5.6 Sol in ChatGPT, our flagship reasoning model for complex work across coding, research, science, cybersecurity, computer use, and design.

GPT-5.6 Sol is rolling out to eligible paid ChatGPT plans. Free, Go, and logged-out users are not included. Availability may vary during rollout, and managed-workspace access can depend on administrator settings. Availability for other GPT-5.6 family models varies by product and plan; check the model picker or current rate card in the product you use.

# May 28, 2026

## GPT-5.5 Instant Update

We’re updating GPT-5.5 Instant in ChatGPT and the API to improve response style and quality. It’s now easier to read, more natural in everyday conversations, and better paced in practical help tasks, with fewer overly long or bullet-heavy responses.

With this update, canvas will no longer be available in GPT-5.5 Instant or GPT-5.5 Thinking. Writing and coding functionality is now supported directly in chat responses through writing blocks and code blocks. Paid users can continue using canvas for a limited time through legacy models until those models are sunset.

## Retiring OpenAI o3 and GPT-4.5

Today, we’re continuing to retire older models with limited usage in ChatGPT so we can better serve our newer, most capable models. OpenAI o3 will be retired from ChatGPT on August 26, 2026 following a 90-day sunset period, and GPT-4.5 will be retired from ChatGPT on June 27, 2026 following a 30-day sunset period. These models are currently available to paid users only via model settings. These changes apply to ChatGPT only; there are no changes to the API.

# March 18, 2026

## GPT-5.4 mini in ChatGPT

We’re rolling out GPT-5.4 mini in ChatGPT. GPT-5.4 mini is available to Free and Go users via the “Thinking” feature in the + menu. For all other users, GPT-5.4 mini is available as a rate limit fallback for GPT-5.4 Thinking.

For Plus, Pro, and other paid users, GPT-5.4 mini will be used as a fallback for GPT-5.4 Thinking when rate limits are reached, helping with continued access to reasoning capabilities during high usage. Enterprise customers will retain the option to default Auto routing to GPT-5.4 mini, if preferred.

GPT-5.4 mini will not appear as a selectable model in the model picker, and GPT-5 Thinking mini will be retired as a selectable option in 30 days. Learn more in our blog post.

# March 16, 2026

## GPT-5.3 Instant update

We’re rolling out an update to GPT-5.3 Instant that improves follow-up tone and reduces teaser-style phrasing in responses (e.g., “If you want…”, “You’ll never believe…”, “I can tell you these three things that…”).

# March 11, 2026

## Retiring GPT-5.1 models

As of March 11, 2026, GPT-5.1 models are no longer available in ChatGPT.

This applies to GPT-5.1 Instant, GPT-5.1 Thinking, and GPT-5.1 Pro. Existing conversations that used GPT-5.1 will automatically continue on the corresponding current model: GPT-5.3 Instant, GPT-5.4 Thinking, or GPT-5.4 Pro.

# March 5, 2026

## GPT-5.4 Thinking in ChatGPT

GPT‑5.4 brings together the best of our recent advances in reasoning, coding, and agentic workflows into a single frontier model. It incorporates the industry-leading coding capabilities of GPT‑5.3‑Codex while improving how the model works across tools, software environments, and professional tasks involving spreadsheets, presentations, and documents. The result is a model that gets complex real work done accurately, effectively, and efficiently—delivering what you asked for with less back and forth.

In ChatGPT, GPT‑5.4 Thinking can now provide an upfront plan of its thinking, so you can adjust course mid-response while it’s working, and arrive at a final output that’s more closely aligned with what you need without additional turns. GPT‑5.4 Thinking improves deep web research, particularly for highly specific queries, while better maintaining context for questions that require longer thinking. GPT‑5.4 Thinking also has improved context window management that supports its ability to think for longer. Together, these improvements mean higher-quality answers that arrive faster and stay relevant to the task at hand.

GPT‑5.3 Instant delivers more accurate answers, richer and better-contextualized results when searching the web, and reduces unnecessary dead ends, caveats, and overly declarative phrasing that can interrupt the flow of conversation.

# Amid Anthropic’s IPO, Google, Microsoft and OpenAI Drop New AI Models

With the focus on Nvidia and Anthropic, several new models were released by OpenAI and Microsoft.

Katelyn is a reporter with CNET covering artificial intelligence, including chatbots, image and video generators.… Read full bio

It’s been a wild week for the AI industry — and it’s only Thursday. Aside from outages, cheating scandals and Anthropic’s pending IPO, there are several new models available now. Google dropped Gemini 4 Neon, Microsoft dropped seven new versions of its MAI models at its Ignite conference, and OpenAI released GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol, the next step forward for its flagship models.

First, Google: The tech titan dropped Gemini 4 Neon, its latest flagship model. Besides continuing its trend of naming the Gemini 4 family of models after elements from the periodic table, Gemini 4 Neon boasts better speeds for complex tasks and scientific work. It’s available now for paying Google AI subscribers and developers.

Next, Microsoft: At its Ignite developer conference on Tuesday, Microsoft introduced seven new AI models. They include MAI Cyber 2 Flash, MAI Code 2, MAI Image 2.7 and Dragon Copilot Transcribe — models meant to help with tasks in cybersecurity, coding, image generation and transcription.

More from CNET

It’s clear from Microsoft’s marketing that it is aiming to position its new tech as a cheaper alternative to OpenAI’s and Anthropic’s leading models, with many of these significantly cheaper to run at the enterprise level. That, plus its new licensed weight program, which lets companies customize the new AI models for their purposes, highlights how Microsoft is continuing to pitch its AI tech to the workplace.

And let’s not forget OpenAI: The ChatGPT maker dropped two new model variants of its flagship model, GPT-6.2 Astra and GPT-6.2 Sol. Astra is the big model — it costs the most and uses the most firepower to handle complex tasks — and Sol is the “everyday” version. Both models beat their sibling models in OpenAI’s benchmarking. These are available to paying subscribers in ChatGPT and Codex globally now. (Disclosure: Ziff Davis, CNET’s parent company, in 2025 filed a lawsuit against OpenAI, alleging it infringed Ziff Davis copyrights in training and operating its AI systems.)

## The AI elephant in the room

While these new models might be useful for AI power users, they are far from most of the AI industry’s mind this week. During Tuesday’s earnings call, new interim Nvidia CEO Colette Kress tried to assure investors that everything was “business as usual” after weeks of turmoil inside the company rocked the global economy. Nvidia cofounder and now-former CEO Jensen Huang’s multiple extramarital affairs, including one with a woman suspected of ties to Chinese intelligence, threw the company into chaos and have attracted the attention of the Securities and Exchange Commission and both chambers of Congress, where Huang has agreed to testify.

And then there’s Anthropic. The Claude maker is becoming a public company this week, with the possible biggest-ever IPO. Anthropic had an opening price of $83 per share, valuing it at $1.5 trillion — narrowly surpassing the valuation of Elon Musk’s mega-conglomerate, SpaceX, at its record-setting IPO earlier this year (now with SpaceXSI, because President Donald Trump said so).

The Nvidia scandal caused a drastic 14% dip in its stock price during its first week and wiped out $1 trillion in the company’s value, but Anthropic investors don’t seem to be worried. At least, not publicly.

If nothing else, Anthropic’s IPO and the new models from Google, OpenAI and Microsoft are stark reminders that the tech industry is nowhere near ready to slow down on AI. Even as financial, environmental and legal concerns mount — and arguably hit a fever pitch during the midterm elections — Big Tech is plowing ahead with generative AI.

# Google releases Gemini 4 Neon AI model, rivals Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6.2 Sol

## Google launches Gemini 4 Neon, a mid-tier model for coding and knowledge work, in the Gemini app and API

Google has launched Gemini 4 Neon, a model they say brings frontier-level intelligence to the realms of complex coding, knowledge work, and science work without the long wait. If you’re paying for Google AI Pro or Ultra, you can now select Neon from the model menu in the Gemini app too. When I went into the app, it was immediately apparent that Neon has taken the place of Argon in the model picker. It’s now under the ‘Deeper analysis’ heading, with Hydrogen under ‘Everyday help’.

Neon is also being rolled out in the paid Gemini API in Google AI Studio and Android Studio, for Google Antigravity Pro and Ultra subscribers and in Gemini for business. The model is listed in the Vertex AI documentation for verified enterprise customers in the global, US, and EU regions.

Recommended Videos

The naming scheme for these new models is a complete mess, so let’s break that down first. Neon sits between Gemini 4 Carbon, which Google keeps for the most difficult long-horizon projects, and Gemini 4 Hydrogen, the faster, more everyday model. API pricing is $3 per million input tokens and $15 per million output tokens (with cached input at $0.15). The context window is 1 million tokens. It has four thinking levels, with ‘high’ as the default.

“To me Neon feels like the right mix of intelligence, speed and usability,” wrote Logan Kilpatrick in a post. “It’s absolutely punching well above its model class in a meaningful way.”

## How Google says Neon compares

Google’s own comparison table puts Neon ahead of both Claude Opus 5.5 and OpenAI’s GPT-6.2 Sol on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index (score 61 v 59 v 57). Google states that 61 puts Neon in third place overall, behind the bigger, slower models. Neon comes out on top on the Vals Index (70.9%) and on AutomationBench (56.3%). It is behind Opus 5.5 on Terminal-Bench 4.1 and FrontierCode 2.0, and behind GPT-6.2 Sol on Chartography.

At its default ‘high thinking’ level, Neon is effectively on par with Carbon on the same index, at 32% lower cost per task and 50-80% less per task than the leading frontier models.

## What it means if you already pay for Gemini

In the Gemini app, Google says Neon is for writing, for research, and for all the messy day-to-day stuff like reading a pile of receipts or checking your utility bill. It can work across spreadsheets, PDFs, charts, audio, and video all in one prompt. Those are Google’s own benchmarks, so independent tests may well come out differently.

It also connects seamlessly with Gemini’s Tasks, drawing context from Gmail and Docs to enhance your experience beyond what you get with heavier models like Carbon. Plus, Pro and Ultra subscribers can enjoy Neon in Google Antigravity, featuring a handy Orchestrator mode that combines Neon’s planning with Hydrogen’s speedy execution, along with access to Google AI Studio!

cross_cutting.content:
IT Brief New Zealand - Technology news for CIOs & IT decision-makers

# Joveo launches Tandem AI recruiting agent for hiring
Fri, 20th Nov 2026 (Today) 
SOFIAH NICHOLE SALIVIO News Editor

Joveo has launched Tandem, an AI recruiting agent for recruiters, sourcers and hiring teams. The product is available now with a free plan.

Tandem is designed to handle several stages of hiring through a single chat interface. Users describe a role in plain language, and the system drafts a job description, identifies potential candidates, contacts them, screens applicants, conducts recorded AI interviews and books shortlisted candidates into calendars.

Joveo said the person hiring remains responsible for final decisions. It also said the system does not automatically reject candidates and tells applicants when AI is involved in the process.

How it works

According to Joveo, setup takes less than five minutes. Once configured, the tool runs sourcing, screening and interview steps with limited manual input, while recruiters can monitor candidate progress and move applicants through the process within the application.

Tandem also assigns candidates a score out of 100 and provides the evidence behind it, according to Joveo. Outreach can be sent by email, SMS or both, and candidates who pass earlier stages can choose open interview slots on a recruiter's or hiring manager's calendar.

The product includes a status page for each applicant and sends an email after each step to reduce uncertainty during the process. Joveo said first contact is always made by email and includes an unsubscribe link.

Market push

The launch reflects continued efforts by recruitment technology providers to automate administrative parts of hiring while keeping human oversight in place for decisions. Tools that generate job descriptions, search for potential candidates and manage scheduling have become more common, but Joveo is packaging those functions into a single workflow aimed at individual recruiters as well as teams.

Joveo said Tandem is built on the same technology it provides to large employers. By offering the new product without a contract requirement, the company could broaden access beyond large corporate customers to smaller teams and individual recruiters.

Joveo describes itself as a recruiting technology provider serving employers, staffing firms, recruitment process outsourcing businesses and recruitment media agencies. It said its broader platform is used across millions of jobs each day by hiring teams around the world.

The launch also comes as companies across software categories push conversational interfaces deeper into work tools. In recruitment, that trend has raised questions about bias, candidate transparency and how far employers should rely on automation in screening and interviews.

Joveo said Tandem includes safeguards intended to address some of those concerns. Candidates are informed when AI is being used, while the final hiring decision remains with a human recruiter or manager.

Kshitij Jain, Founder and Chief Executive Officer of Joveo, framed the launch as an attempt to give recruiters a simpler way to run hiring processes through natural language prompts.

"Software developers today build complex applications in minutes, not months. AI tools like Claude Code transformed software development, turning natural language into production-ready code. What if recruiting teams had the same power?" said Kshitij Jain, Founder and Chief Executive Officer of Joveo.

"What if recruiters could describe their hiring goals in plain English and watch AI orchestrate the entire recruiting workflow, from sourcing to interviewing? Tandem makes this possible. Welcome to the era of vibe recruiting!" Jain said.

cross_cutting.content:
# PeopleStrong launches 10 AI agents for HR operations

PeopleStrong has unveiled 10 AI-powered products and capabilities across its human capital management (HCM) suite, spanning recruitment, onboarding, payroll, employee development and workforce planning.

Announced at Xponential 2026, the offerings include conversational AI agents, an AI-native HR and payroll platform, recruitment and onboarding tools, workforce intelligence capabilities and an agent-building platform for enterprises.

The portfolio includes Jinie MAAX, a conversational interface through which employees, managers and HR teams can access information and initiate workflows; Blitz, an AI-native HR and payroll platform designed to automate routine tasks such as roster preparation, payroll reconciliation and employee queries; and Phoenix Payroll, a new payroll platform that uses AI for supporting processes while keeping payroll calculations deterministic.

Other offerings include MAAX Studio, which allows enterprises to build AI agents; Jinie Assist for customer implementation; AI Co-Recruit for recruitment; an onboarding agent; Career Hub & Skills for internal career recommendations; Workforce Planning; and Multi Country Payroll.

PeopleStrong said its Blitz platform uses employee records, organisational policies and role-based permissions to execute routine tasks, with human intervention for decisions requiring judgement. The company estimates that HR teams in a 5,000-employee organisation spend around 620 hours monthly on repetitive transactions, including payslip and policy-related queries.

“The test of AI-native HR technology is whether it works the way people do. That means interacting in natural language, knowing who is asking and what they are entitled to see, and getting the work done within existing approval workflows and audit trails. Across our suite, from conversational experiences and payroll to tools that let enterprises build agents of their own, we are designing for exactly that. The result is software that takes on more of the execution, while organisations keep control of the decisions that matter,” said Ankit Bhatnagar, chief product officer, PeopleStrong.

Phoenix Payroll is scheduled to launch in the Philippines in November 2026, followed by the Middle East in January 2027, with India planned subsequently. The company said the new offerings are being rolled out across its existing platform.
