# Hitachi Digital launches HARC Compose to help enterprises manage AI agents

The platform helps organisations build, deploy, and manage AI agents while maintaining human oversight of critical decisions.

Hitachi Digital on Thursday said it has launched HARC Compose, a unified product combining technology and services to help enterprises govern the lifecycle of agentic engineering across complex, AI-driven systems.

According to the official press release, the platform uses enterprise-specific business context, policies and guardrails to coordinate AI execution across development, deployment, operations and continuous improvement. It is designed to help organisations build, deploy and manage AI agents while maintaining human oversight of critical decisions.

Hitachi Digital's forward deployed engineers (FDEs) will use HARC Compose to develop AI-native applications and continuously maintain and improve deployed agents' performance. The product is compatible with multi-vendor environments, allowing enterprises to use the complete platform or select individual capabilities based on their requirements.

HARC Compose also strengthens HMAX by Hitachi, a suite of solutions bringing AI to social infrastructure. It complements HMAX Foundry solutions, including HMAX Data Fabric, HMAX AI Operations and HMAX Cyber.

“By bringing our engineering and operational expertise together, HARC Compose allows clients to innovate at AI speed while running what they build with proven reliability,” said Anand Birje, CEO and Chairman, Hitachi Digital.

The platform includes three key capabilities. Its Context-Aware Knowledge Engine (CAKE) connects enterprise objectives, domain knowledge, systems, policies, security requirements and production history, while identifying gaps and contradictions before AI agents act. An orchestration engine coordinates multiple agents across development, deployment, and operations, and supports customer-selected tools without requiring them to replace existing coding or development environments.

### FMEA-based approach identifies risks before deployment
Its failure-conscious engineering capability uses failure mode and effects analysis to identify potential risks in proposed changes and translate them into tests, controls and recovery strategies. The platform also offers guided and autonomous work modes, allowing engineers to review decisions before agent action or monitor agents operating within agreed limits.
HARC Compose is built on Hitachi Digital's outcome-forward engineering methodology, which treats defining, building, deploying and operating systems as a continuous process. Under this approach, delivery is considered complete when the system achieves its intended business outcomes in real-world operations.

The platform is available to enterprises worldwide, with deployments supported by Hitachi Digital's FDEs already underway in the finance, healthcare and technology sectors.

# Siemens launches Eigen Engineering Agent in India, says it frees up humans for complex work

## Siemens has brought its Eigen Engineering Agent to India. The company says Eigen can carry out tasks and accelerate development while freeing engineers to do higher-skilled work.

Advertisement

Siemens' Eigen Engineering Agent is designed to automate tasks in real world systems. (Photo: Siemens)

Siemens has brought its Eigen Engineering Agent to India. The agent is designed to automate repetitive tasks for clients that could free humans for more complex work, the company said. Ahead of the launch, Eigen was piloted by 16 Siemens clients in India.

As per the company, Eigen is an industrial AI agent that is built for real engineering systems. The agent can carry out certain tasks autonomously, such as PLC coding and Human-Machine-Interface (HMI) visualisation, while meeting industrial standards for safety.

advertisement

While AI and automation has become a focus for industries globally, there has been a fear of reduced roles for humans. Siemen says Eigen frees up engineers for “higher-level system challenges” by automating certain tasks. Eigen can do tasks two to five times faster than manual alternatives as per the company. While Eigen can do tasks autonomously, humans remain responsible for final deployment.

While Eigen is now available in India, the AI agent was already available in other markets. During a media briefing, Siemens confirmed that Eigen was one of its fastest growing SaaS products in regions where it was available.

Siemens AG CTO Dr Dirk Didascalou said that Eigen can help accelerate growth in India as it gives engineers more time to work on innovation. “By bringing AI directly into the engineering workflow, it can help engineers manage complexity, work faster and spend more time on innovation,” he said. “This is how we translate research into practical solutions that can strengthen competitiveness and accelerate India’s industrial transformation.”

With Eigen, Siemens is also focusing on small and medium enterprises who can access the agent via the company’s existing TIA Portal. “India’s next manufacturing leap will be driven by productivity and quality, not just cost. For that, automation must reach the entire value chain, especially small and medium enterprises,” Siemens India CEO Sunil Mathur said. “The Eigen Engineering Agent makes this possible.”

In pilot results shared by Siemens, organisations saw the agent cut repetitive engineering work by more than 50 per cent and improve productivity by 20 to 30 per cent in certain cases. The agent was launched during Transform – Siemens India Innovation Day in New Delhi.

## TMCnet News

## Wallarm Launches Agentic Operators: AI Agents That Run Application Security, With Your Team in Control

Wallarm today launched Agentic Operators, AI agents built into the Wallarm platform that investigate threats, resolve false positives, tune security policies, and report on security posture using live application and API traffic. Because Wallarm sits inline, Agentic Operators act on the same rules that block live traffic, taking routine security operations work off overstretched teams. Configurable autonomy keeps people in control of the decisions that matter.

The capacity gap in application security

Attackers are exploiting weaknesses faster than security teams can investigate them. For the first time in the report's 19-year history, vulnerability exploitation is the leading way into a breach, behind 31% of breaches, according to the 2026 Verizon Data Breach Investigations Report. The same report finds AI is shrinking the time to exploit known vulnerabilities from months to hours.

Budgets aren't keeping pace. The 2026 IANS and Artico Search Security Budget Benchmark Report found 55% of organizations held security budgets flat or cut them this year. In the same study, 69% of CISOs named AI for security their top priority for new spending, and 91% expect AI to make their security teams more productive over the next 12 months.

Most application security tools detect threats, enforce rules, and raise alerts. Someone still has to investigate each alert, decide whether it matters, and fix the rule behind it. AI assistants explain what's happening, but stop short of acting. Workflow automation acts, but only on steps people build and maintain. Agentic Operators close that gap by doing the work.

"Security teams don't need another stream of alerts. They need the work behind those alerts to get done," said Shayne Higdon, CEO, Wallarm. "Agentic Operators investigate, decide, and act inside the platform that already sees your traffic. Most AI in security tells you what to fix. These operators fix it, and they learn from every decision your team makes so protecton gets tighter over time. Agent-run, team-approved."

Meet the team

Agentic Operators work from the real-time traffic Wallarm already inspects. Each operator owns a defined part of security operations, and all of them learn from the outcomes of their decisions.

Team captain

- Wally leads the team. It's the AI interface security teams use to work with Wallarm: ask what happened, review and approve what the operators did, and handle configuration requests and routine platform tasks in plain language.

Threat response

- Radar investigates sudden spikes in attack activity, explains what is behind them, and proposes and implements blocking rules and mitigation controls.
- Sift tells real attacks from false alarms and corrects the rules behind false positives, cutting alert noise and unnecessary blocking.

Platform operations

- Tune continuously reviews security policies and recommends improvements, so protection stays effective with less manual work.
- Trim keeps the ruleset lean, so request processing and rule updates stay fast.

Posture and reporting

- Lens reviews API inventory, exposures, and vulnerabilities to surface the risks that matter without constant manual checks.
- Bard summarizes security activity, changes, and outstanding risks so leaders can see results and set priorities.

Teams set autonomy per application and per remediation action. They can require approval for every action, only for sensitive changes, or not at all, and change that setting as trust builds. Through Wallarm's MCP server, security teams can integrate these Agentic Operators with their own AI agents.

"Managing WAF false positives usually means constant manual rule tuning," said Muhammad Irfan, Director of DevOps & Infrastructure at a global virtual events platform. "Wallarm's Agentic Operators take that operational tax off our plate by filtering out false alarms automatically so our team can stay focused on real threats."

What comes next

Agentic Operators are the first step toward next-generation application security that runs itself. Wallarm's new platform, built for agents to operate, is planned for general availability in early 2027. Traditional application security solutions were built for people to configure, one rule at a time. The new platform is built for agents to do that work: read live traffic, change a policy, test the change against real attacks, and roll back if something breaks, with every action logged for the security team to review. Customers using Agentic Operators today will carry them forward to the new platform.

Availability

Seven Agentic Operators are available today, covering anomaly detection, false positive remediation, and platform tuning. Agentic Operators for red teaming and virtual patching will be available for early access in early 2027. Learn more at https://www.wallarm.com/product/agentic-operators.

Wallarm at AWS re:Invent 2026

Wallarm will demonstrate Agentic Operators in Las Vegas, November 30 to December 4, at Booth 345 in the Venetian. To schedule a meeting or request a demo, visit https://www.wallarm.com/events/aws-reinvent-2026.

About Wallarm

Wallarm is the AI-native application security platform, built for agentic operators. It blocks attacks in real time across every API, application, and AI workload in production. Organizations choose Wallarm for a complete inventory of APIs, AI agents, and AI apps, and patented ML-based threat detection and blocking that operates at production traffic speeds. Wallarm is headquartered in Austin, Texas, and is backed by Toba Capital, Y Combinator, and other investors. https://www.wallarm.com

# UC Berkeley, Berkeley Lab collaboration with Schmidt Science Computing Network will Provide High Performance Computing for Cutting-Edge Research

By Bob Sanders and Elizabeth Ball

New tools for super intelligence (SI), commonly referred to as artificial intelligence, are rapidly accelerating scientific discovery, but researchers’ ambitions often exceed computing capacity.

To expand the advanced computing available for science, the University of California, Berkeley and Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory (Berkeley Lab) will join the Schmidt Science Computing Network (SSCN), a new distributed network of institution-owned computing systems designed to help scientists tackle complex challenges at previously unreachable scales.

“UC Berkeley and Berkeley Lab have been driving discovery together for nearly a century,” said Rich Lyons, UC Berkeley’s chancellor. “Now, with Schmidt Sciences, our researchers have the computing power they need to cast new light on even more of science’s biggest questions. I can’t wait to see the discoveries enabled as a result.”

A major grant from Schmidt Sciences will establish the Berkeley Science AI Platform (BSAIP) that will run on hardware at the National Energy Research Scientific Computing Center (NERSC), a scientific user facility at Berkeley Lab, which is owned by the U.S. Department of Energy (DOE). BSAIP is the first academic-philanthropic public-private collaboration in the DOE ecosystem.

The goal of SSCN is to pair institution-owned and/or operated, frontier-class compute infrastructure with expert support, software, and a shared scientific purpose so researchers can pursue work at a scale that has historically been inaccessible to many individual academic teams. SSCN is a part of the philanthropic organization Schmidt Sciences founded by former Google CEO Eric Schmidt and Wendy Schmidt. Their support has funded researchers across the globe in computer science, astrophysics, biosciences, climate, and science systems.

Support through SSCN will enable BSAIP to add compute and storage to Doudna, NERSC’s new flagship supercomputer named for Nobel Prize-winning Berkeley chemist Jennifer Doudna. Powered by ORv3 direct liquid-cooled Dell PowerEdge servers technology from Dell Technologies in combination with NVIDIA’s groundbreaking Vera Rubin platform, the system will be engineered to support large-scale high performance computing and provide a robust environment for the workflows that make cutting-edge science possible, scheduled for availability to users in 2028. Within the BSAIP allocation, dedicated capacity is intended to be allocated to Schmidt Sciences awardees and also to UC Berkeley for the university’s researchers.

“NERSC’s mission is to provide advanced computing systems and services for scientific discovery, bringing science solutions to the world through computing,” said Berkeley Lab Director Kathy Yelick. “This system will leverage the Doudna system architecture and contribute to the DOE’s Genesis Mission by broadening access to advanced computing for current and future machine learning applications. It will help advance human knowledge and accelerate discovery.”

“I’m excited to see how researchers across the disciplines will use this new resource once it comes online. Schmidt Sciences has been an important partner to leading researchers around the world and we are delighted to have the opportunity to support their success as part of this unique public-private collaboration,” added Vice Chancellor for Research Richard Allen.

The Schmidt Science Computing Network’s goal is not simply to provide hardware, but to build scientific capability, software and expertise that can endure over time.

“Scientific ambition should not be limited by whether a research team already has the massive computing and storage needed to pursue its most important questions,” said Schmidt Sciences President Stuart Feldman. “The Schmidt Science Computing Network is a bet on the ingenuity of scientists and the strength of research institutions. By pairing advanced computing with expert support and durable software, we can help researchers work at new scales advancing discoveries that benefit society.”

Scheduled for deployment in 2027, Doudna will support cutting-edge research across fields such as cosmology, genome engineering, earth science, materials science, and computational biology. NERSC already counts among its users many prominent researchers, including Berkeley Nobel Laureates Doudna and Saul Perlmutter, whose groundbreaking work could benefit from increased compute capacity on the Doudna system. Increased compute capacity will enable the use of next-generation tools that expand and accelerate what these scientists and others can learn and produce in areas like making massive maps of the universe to study dark matter and dark energy, supercharging the process of modeling and discovering innovative new materials, and editing the human genome to prevent and treat a range of health conditions, among many other areas.

"Biology is becoming as much a computational science as an experimental one, and this partnership puts frontier-scale computing to work in the field," said Jennifer Doudna, CRISPR pioneer and founder of the Innovative Genomics Institute at UC Berkeley. "Paired with the right data, that power lets SI surface more possibilities than any lab could test. Choosing which ones to pursue still takes a scientist's judgment and the kind of curiosity that has always driven fundamental research at Berkeley. Researchers who bring both to this system will make breakthroughs across medicine, agriculture, and climate, and find answers none of us can see yet."

Other members in the Schmidt Science Computing Network announced today include the University of Chicago, The University of Illinois, Urbana-Champaign and Johns Hopkins University. For more information about the Schmidt Science Computing Network please visit schmidtsciences.org/sscn.

### About NERSC and Berkeley Lab

The National Energy Research Scientific Computing Center (NERSC) is the mission computing facility for the U.S. Department of Energy Office of Science, the nation’s single largest supporter of basic research in the physical sciences.

Located at Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory (Berkeley Lab), NERSC serves 11,000 scientists at national laboratories and universities researching a wide range of problems in climate, fusion energy, materials sciences, physics, chemistry, computational biology, and other disciplines. An average of 2,000 peer-reviewed science results a year rely on NERSC resources and expertise, which has also supported the work of seven Nobel Prize-winning scientists and teams.

NERSC is a U.S. Department of Energy Office of Science User Facility.

# Firebird expands AI infrastructure in Armenia with Dell Technologies

3 minute read

Firebird is expanding its computing capacity as part of its ongoing collaboration with Dell Technologies, supporting the development of Armenia’s artificial intelligence ecosystem, the company said.

Firebird has completed the first phase of construction of its AI cluster in Hrazdan. The cluster is built around a Dell PowerRack system with Dell PowerEdge servers and NVIDIA Blackwell graphics processing units. Researchers, developers and companies in Armenia and across the region can now work in a fully operational AI environment. The cluster provides the computing power needed for work in life sciences, autonomous systems, space technologies and materials science.

In the next phase, Firebird plans to increase its computing capacity for training and running AI models. The expansion will allow the company to serve corporate customers worldwide on a larger scale from Armenia and strengthen the country’s position as a hub for AI innovation.

“With this agreement, we are continuing our collaboration with Dell Technologies and expanding our ability to provide advanced computing capacity for large-scale AI workloads. We see that emerging markets can play a greater role in meeting global demand for AI. As we build this capacity, we are committed to delivering the quality of service and system reliability that international customers expect and to adhering to responsible business principles. That is how we build lasting trust and secure long-term growth,” said Razmig Hovaghimian, co-founder and CEO of Firebird.

“Firebird and Dell Technologies share the goal of making the computing power needed for AI innovation more accessible. Dell Technologies provides advanced AI systems to organisations around the world. The results of our work together have laid the groundwork for the next phase, which will allow Firebird to serve customers worldwide and help expand Armenia’s role in the AI ecosystem,” said Mohammed Amin, senior vice-president for the CEEMETA region at Dell Technologies.

The expansion is part of Firebird’s long-term plan to build a global AI infrastructure business from Armenia, using its computing capacity to serve AI companies and corporate customers around the world.

# Telia joins European technology leaders in forming AI Gigafactory Northern consortium to build trusted, sustainable AI infrastructure

Press release

Telia, Nokia, Nscale, Verda and Skeleton today announce the formation of AI Gigafactory Northern (AIGF Northern), a European consortium formed to develop trusted, distributed AI infrastructure through a federated, multi-site AI Gigafactory across the Nordic and Baltic region. Operating as a federated AI Gigafactory under European governance, the sites will combine large-scale AI computing infrastructure with sovereign cloud and AI platform services, high-capacity connectivity and decarbonized energy. The partners intend to submit a bid to build and operate AIGF Northern under the call for tenders for AI Gigafactory consortia published by the European High-Performance Computing Joint Undertaking (EuroHPC JU).

AIGF Northern will connect AI infrastructure across multiple sites in the Nordic and Baltic region, giving businesses, researchers and public-sector organizations throughout Europe access to trusted computing, cloud and connectivity services at scale. By distributing capacity across borders, the federated AI Gigafactory will reduce concentration risk and strengthen the resilience of Europe’s AI ecosystem.

The consortium is being developed as the EU steps up investment in European AI capacity. Through InvestAI, the EU aims to mobilize €30 billion for AI investment, combining €20 billion in private-sector funding with €10 billion from EU and national public sources.

AIGF Northern will connect facilities in Oulu, Finland; the Tallinn region in Estonia; Valmiera, Latvia; and a to-be-determined location in Sweden. Distributing capacity across these locations will allow the consortium to draw on multiple sources of decarbonized energy, expand computing infrastructure where capacity is available and reduce reliance on any single site or supplier. This approach will strengthen operational resilience and support cross-border expansion as European demand for AI grows.

Telia, together with its subsidiary Telia Cygate, will contribute expertise in connectivity, data transmission, infrastructure operations and sovereign cloud solutions, supporting the development of a federated, multi-country AI ecosystem.

Anders Olsson, Executive Vice President, Head of Telia Sweden: “Our customers – and our continent – have a rapidly increasing need for scalable and sovereign AI services. To meet this need, Europe’s best must step up. Telia’s highly relevant skills in secure and resilient connectivity and systems integration, combined with our position as a trusted partner for businesses and societies, make us a natural fit for this ambitious consortium. We look forward to working together to create even more value for customers, while helping to secure long-term European competitiveness and resilience.”

Building trusted AI infrastructure for Europe

The Nordic and Baltic region offers suitable conditions for sustainable AI infrastructure, combining reliable, decarbonized energy supply, advanced digital networks and a cool climate that reduces cooling demand. These advantages enable data centers to deliver more computing capacity from existing grid connections while supporting lower-carbon operations.

The consortium is also supported by leading research and innovation partners. VTT Technical Research Centre of Finland, one of Europe’s leading research organizations and a partner for companies and society, brings capabilities in quantum computing, semiconductors, physical AI and photonics.
Telia brings its collaboration with KTH Royal Institute of Technology, Sweden’s largest technical university, to the consortium. KTH will contribute multidisciplinary expertise in AI research, education and skills development. Telia recently signed an MoU with KTH and Brookfield to jointly develop AI services and applications in Sweden. In addition, Telia has a long-term strategic partnership with Brookfield on Sweden’s largest sovereign AI initiative.

Together with other ecosystem partners, VTT and KTH will help connect AIGF Northern’s infrastructure ambitions with Europe’s research, innovation and talent networks.

The consortium aims to create value for industry, start-ups, research organizations and the public sector across Europe. Partners are engaging European and national stakeholders to refine the model and identify next steps for growth.

Consortium founding partners across the value chain

Telia, together with its subsidiary Telia Cygate, contributes expertise in connectivity, data transmission, infrastructure operations and sovereign cloud solutions, supporting the development of a federated, multi-country AI ecosystem.

Nokia provides the secure, high-performance connectivity and network infrastructure needed to link sites, move data reliably and support resilient operations.

Nscale brings cloud platform and AI infrastructure expertise to enable scalable environments for AI training and inference.

Verda provides AI-native infrastructure and cloud expertise to power scalable training and inference.

Skeleton contributes high-power systems that enhance data-center efficiency and stability at scale, reduce strain on the electricity grid and support lower-carbon operations.

NOTES TO EDITORS

For more information, contact Telia’s press office on +46 (0)771 77 58 30, visit our newsroom and follow us on LinkedIn. To download our logo, high-resolution images of Telia leaders, offices and solutions, or B-roll footage for editorial use, visit our media bank.

ABOUT TELIA

Telia (STO: TELIA) is a leading telecommunications operator in the Nordic and Baltic regions. Every day, we deliver world-class connectivity and communications services to millions of customers through our sustainable and secure networks – enabling people, businesses and societies to thrive and grow. Our unique position at the center of digitalization shapes our ambition to be a trusted and progressive partner and gives us our purpose: to reinvent better connected living. Find out more at www.teliacompany.com/en.

ABOUT AI GIGAFACTORY NORTHERN

AI Gigafactory Northern is a European-led consortium advancing a federated, multi-site model for AI infrastructure. Built across the Nordic and Baltic region to serve customers throughout Europe, it brings together capabilities in connectivity, data transmission, energy, cloud, AI systems and delivery to support trusted, scalable and sustainable AI expansion aligned with European priorities. For more information, visit aigfnorthern.com.

cross_cutting.content:
20-year, 10-megawatt agreement underpins deployment of B300 systems for AI inference

SAN FRANCISCO and NEW YORK, November 17, 2026 — Argentum AI, a premium GPU cloud provider, and Kyndryl (NYSE: KD), a leading provider of mission-critical enterprise technology services, today announced a 20-year, $630M data center collaboration for an initial 10 megawatts (MW) of capacity at Kyndryl’s Boulder, Colorado, facility to power deployment of NVIDIA GPU systems.

Argentum is deploying NVIDIA B300 systems at the site in a fully Tier III environment, creating advanced, enterprise-grade infrastructure to run demanding AI applications at scale. Deployment is underway.

The agreement provides Argentum access to a facility built for the power density of current-generation GPU systems and gives Argentum’s customers a faster path to high-performance inference capacity.

“Partnering with an established technology services and infrastructure provider like Kyndryl is an important milestone for Argentum AI,” said Andrew Sobko, Founder and CEO, Argentum AI. “This agreement reflects our shared commitment to expanding secure, high-performance compute infrastructure and supporting the growing demands of enterprises embracing AI at scale.”

“Our agreement gives us a unique opportunity to put Kyndryl capacity to work in an innovative way, this coupled with our mission-critical capabilities, decades of operational and services experience will support Argentum as it creates capacity for its customers,” said Jamie Rutledge, President, Kyndryl U.S.

The facility welcomes a fast-growing, enterprise-grade AI inference company, whose technology powers some of the world’s most widely used AI applications, as its flagship anchor tenant. Argentum AI and Kyndryl intend to broaden their collaboration to support Argentum’s growth and evolving mission-critical enterprise AI infrastructure needs.

About Argentum AI
Argentum AI is a premium GPU cloud provider. The company originates, finances and operates GPU clusters, delivering dedicated bare metal GPU capacity to AI model builders, inference providers and enterprises. Argentum works with data center operators and builds capacity around customer demand, with a focus on speed of delivery, reliability and long-term partnerships. For more information, visit argentum-ai.com.

About Kyndryl
Kyndryl (NYSE: KD) is a leading provider of mission-critical enterprise technology services, offering advisory, implementation and managed service capabilities to thousands of customers in more than 60 countries. As the world’s largest IT infrastructure services provider, the company designs, builds, manages and modernizes the complex information systems that the world depends on every day. For more information, visit www.kyndryl.com.

# Nokia, Telia, and Partners Join Forces to Develop Northern European AI Gigafactory

European technology companies Nokia, Nscale, Skeleton Technologies, Telia, and Verda have formed a consortium to develop AI Gigafactory Northern (AIGF Northern), a federated AI infrastructure project spanning the Nordic and Baltic region. The initiative aims to strengthen Europe’s AI capabilities by combining large-scale computing infrastructure, sovereign cloud services, high-capacity connectivity, and decarbonized energy under European governance.

The founding partners intend to submit a joint bid in response to the European High-Performance Computing Joint Undertaking’s call for tenders for AI Gigafactory consortia. If selected, the project will connect multiple facilities across Northern Europe, providing businesses, researchers, and public-sector organizations throughout the continent with access to trusted AI computing, cloud, and connectivity services.

The planned infrastructure will span Oulu in Finland, Iru in Estonia, and Valmiera in Latvia, while the location of the Swedish site has yet to be determined. By distributing computing capacity across several countries, the consortium aims to reduce dependence on individual facilities and suppliers, strengthen operational resilience, and support the expansion of Europe’s AI ecosystem.

The project comes as the European Union steps up efforts to develop its own AI infrastructure. Through its InvestAI initiative, the EU aims to mobilize EUR 30 billion in investment, combining EUR 20 billion in private-sector funding with EUR 10 billion from EU and national public sources.

The Nordic and Baltic region offers several advantages for large-scale AI infrastructure, including access to reliable, decarbonized electricity, advanced digital networks, and a cooler climate that can reduce data center cooling requirements. These conditions could help improve energy efficiency and enable facilities to deliver greater computing capacity using existing grid connections.

“Europe’s AI ambitions depend on infrastructure it can trust, control, and scale. AIGF Northern brings together the connectivity, computing, cloud, and energy capabilities needed to turn that ambition into reality. By linking strengths across borders, we can build a more resilient foundation for European innovation, competitiveness, and technological sovereignty,” said Mikko Hautala, Chief Geopolitical and Government Relations Officer and Chairman of Nokia Defense.

Each founding partner will contribute a different part of the infrastructure value chain. Nokia will provide secure, high-performance connectivity and network infrastructure, while Nscale will bring cloud platform capabilities and expertise in AI infrastructure for training and inference. Telia, together with its subsidiary Telia Cygate, will contribute connectivity, data transmission, infrastructure operations, and cloud solutions. Verda will provide AI-native infrastructure and cloud expertise, while Skeleton Technologies will supply high-power systems designed to improve data center efficiency and stability, reduce pressure on electricity grids, and support lower-carbon operations.

The consortium will also draw on expertise from research and innovation organizations. VTT Technical Research Center of Finland will contribute capabilities in quantum computing, semiconductors, physical AI, and photonics, while Sweden’s KTH Royal Institute of Technology will support AI research, education, and skills development. Their involvement will connect the infrastructure project with Europe’s wider research, innovation, and talent ecosystems.
